Sports.title: Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi let himself down – failure to call out Argentina is an insult to football

Lionel Messi has come under fire for failing to condemn Argentina’s physical approach during the World Cup.

The South Americans were at the centre of various controversies during the tournament due to perceived over-physical tactics resulting in a number of tense confrontations.

5 Lionel Messi and Argentina hardly covered themselves in glory during the World Cup final Credit: AFP

5 Leandro Paredes aggressively hit out at Gavi after the final whistle Credit: Getty

Argentina have long adopted football’s dark arts in a bid to gain a psychological advantage over their opponents.

And that’s despite historically producing some of world football’s greatest-ever talents.

Lionel Scaloni’s men were far from their best at the World Cup, often relying on the Messi's wizardry to pull themselves out of the mire.

They were taken to extra time by minnows Cape Verde in the round of 32 before a miraculous late turnaround against Egypt in the last 16.

They were taken to extra time once more in an ill-tempered quarter-final with Switzerland before breaking English hearts in a frantic final ten minutes to book their spot in the final.

But it was the 1-0 defeat against Spain in the final where ten-man Argentina showed themselves in a negative light.

Enzo Fernandez was given his marching orders in the second half before teammates Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes were seen manhandling multiple Spain players after the final whistle.

Their classless antics continued into the trophy presentation where all but one Argentina player turned their backs on Spain's trophy lift.

Former Chelsea striker Tony Cascarino cast his expert eye over Argentina’s fortunes during the World Cup and expressed his disappointment at the incidents.

While Messi opted to distance himself from the on-field controversies, Cascarino believes the 39-year-old should have addressed the behaviour of his teammates in his post-World Cup Instagram post thanking fans for their support.

5 Argentina players couldn't bring themselves to watch Spain lift the trophy Credit: Getty

5 Tony Cascarino spoke of his disappointment at Messi's failure to address his side's antics

Lack of leadership

"They've got some really good players in their squad,” Cascarino said on the Sports Breakfast.

"I was a bit disappointed in Lionel Messi if I'm honest about not actually reacting to the way they played.

"Because he's been the highest [best] player I could ever think of – top notch.

"And would Johan Cruyff have accepted the Netherlands playing that way?

"No, he wouldn't have, he wouldn't have accepted it as the great player that he was, and there's other greats along the way.

"I was surprised that Lionel Messi didn't sort of say, 'Hey, look, physicality is part of our game, but we've got a lot of talent and we should have shown a bit more of that.'

5 A tearful Messi faced up the reality that he may never don the Argentina shirt again Credit: Getty

"Now I know that won them the game against England.

"But I just felt that he's been that good, is he comfortable with Argentina really playing that way?"

Messi broke down in tears after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat.

The Inter Miami star is expected to call time on his international career following 207 caps and 125 goals for La Albiceleste.

In a heartfelt post to his 515 million Instagram followers, he wrote:"The pain is immense, and it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also choose to hold on to all the good things … the matches we played, giving everything we had, will stay in our memories forever.

“With the support of an entire country, together with the hard work and effort of this group, we once again managed to be among the best teams in the world.

“Today it's difficult to fully appreciate what we achieved, but this team reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message.

“Once again, we came together as a country, united by immense pride of being Argentine. I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship."

Sports.title: Eddie Howe ‘doesn’t know’ if Bruno Guimaraes will stay despite ‘good conversations’ at Newcastle
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe ‘doesn’t know’ if Bruno Guimaraes will stay despite ‘good conversations’ at Newcastle

Eddie Howe has admitted his uncertainty over the future of Bruno Guimaraes at Newcastle United this summer.

talkSPORT understands the Brazilian has agreed personal terms with Arsenal ahead of a potential move.

2 Guimaraes continues to be linked with an exit to Arsenal Credit: Getty

Arsenal are also set to face no competition from rival clubs for the 28-year-old, who has two years left on his contract at St. James' Park.

Guimaraes is keen to move to the Premier League champions, who are on course to make a bid north of £70million for his signature.

An exit would come as a significant blow to Newcastle ahead of the new season.

Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have already left for Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur respectively.

Howe has addressed the speculation over his club captain, with he and fans being left in the dark about whether he stays or goes.

"I've spoken to Bruno before, during and after the World Cup," he said via Keith Downie after a 1-1 pre-season friendly draw with Gateshead.

"We have had some really good conversations. He's just a fantastic person.

"I don't know what’s going to happen with his future, that's for other people to speculate about. There's conversations I'm not part of."

Howe added: "I don’t think it's fair to compare (to Alexander Isak last summer). You've got to look at it in its own right.

"He's captain of our club and been an unbelievable player, through the whole time we have worked together.

2 Howe is not sure if his captain will stay at the club beyond the summer Credit: Getty

"I speak on behalf of everyone at the club, we absolutely love him and of course everyone would love him to stay.

"He's due back on the 31st (July), and there's nothing to say he won't be back."

Newcastle reinforcements

Although Guimaraes could follow Gordon and Tonali out of the exit door, Newcastle have been busy with their recruitment.

Ewen Jaouen was their first arrival in an £18m move from Reims, and then Bazoumana Toure joined from TSG Hoffenheim for £43m.

Newcastle have also brought in Sean Steur from Ajax in a deal worth around £23m.

Their latest signing was announced on Friday, with Aladji Bamba making the move from AS Monaco for £34m.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi issues stern message to Tottenham star Lucas Bergvall with talks planned
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has scheduled talks with Lucas Bergvall but insists the door is open for any player wanting to leave Tottenham.

The Sweden international has informed Tottenham chiefs of his desire to find a new club this summer after failing to hold down a spot in the starting XI.

3 Lucas Bergvall sees his immediate future away from Tottenham Credit: Getty

Bergvall, who represented Sweden at the World Cup, has cut short his summer break to join his Spurs teammates on the club’s pre-season tour of Australia and New Zealand.

However, his future remains uncertain with five weeks remaining in the transfer window.

Speaking at his first press conference in Auckland, De Zerbi made his stance clear on players who may be plotting a future away from the club.

“Listen, I was very clear at the start of my time in Tottenham. I said 'Who doesn't want to stay in Tottenham, who is not happy, is not proud to stay here, has to leave,'” the Italian told reporters.

“I want proud players who are happy to stay here and to go on the pitch at Tottenham Stadium with a big motivation.

“If you think also in the World Cup, the motivation makes the difference. The motivation is to be happy to stay in one team.”

Planned talks

Asked specifically about Bergvall’s future, he added: “I have not spoken with Lucas yet, I will in the next days.

“We will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us. Without problems, Lucas is a big, big talent.

“There will be a big competition to play because at the end I think we will have two players for each position.

“If he wants to stay, I will be happy. Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with Johan Lange, with Vinai (Venkatesham). It's not my business after the decision to leave (if that happens).

3 Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi told reporters he is due to have sit down talks with Bergvall in the coming days Credit: Getty

There has been plenty of Premier League interest in Bergvall this summer.

Nottingham Forest made their intentions known but saw their advances rebuffed.

Newcastle went a step further by tabling a £46million offer for the 20-year-old only to see their bid rejected.

It remains to be seen whether Bergvall will secure a move away from Tottenham before deadline day with Spurs holding out for £50m for the Swede.

De Zerbi to prioritise his attack

Elsewhere, De Zerbi revealed that focus would be switched to bolstering his attack ahead of the new season.

Spurs have been active in the transfer market with the signings of defenders Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson.

3 The Swede's hopes of pinning down a first-team spot have taken a huge blow following Spurs' summer shopping spree Credit: Getty

De Zerbi has also strengthened his midfield options after landing Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes for a combined £185m.

And now the Italian has confirmed that he is on the look out for attacking reinforcements.

“The target now is to complete the attacking positions,” he said.

“We want the first target, the first level, because we have already important players.

“But I think to start a new project we need another couple of important players for sure.”

Tottenham’s two-game tour sees them take on Auckland FC at 4am on Sunday morning (UK time).

They then head to Australia to play Sydney FC on Wednesday morning at 10.45am (UK time).

Sports.title: Chelsea reject third bid for Trevoh Chalobah as club refuse to budge on £35m price tag
Sports.content:
Chelsea reject third bid for Trevoh Chalobah as club refuse to budge on £35m price tag

Chelsea have rejected a third transfer bid from Como for Trevoh Chalobah, talkSPORT understands.

The centre-back has been a major target for the Italian club, whose coach is former Blues star Cesc Fabregas.



4 Trevoh Chalobah has been on Chelsea's books for his entire career Credit: Getty

However, their efforts to sign Chalobah have been unsuccessful so far, with Chelsea sticking to their £30million plus £5m asking price.

In June, Como submitted a bid worth more than £22m for Chalobah, which was knocked back.

And whilst they have held advanced talks, the 27-year-old remains a Blues player.



talkSPORT previously reported that the Premier League giants were prepared to sell Chalobah, and a departure now appears more likely as they close in on the signing of Maxence Lacroix.

The Crystal Palace man is expected to arrive at Stamford Bridge in a deal worth north of £55m.



Lacroix's arrival would push Chalobah further down the pecking order in west London, who does not appear part of new boss Xabi Alonso's plans.

The 27-year-old has two years left on a long-term contract signed in 2022, which includes an option to extend it for another 12 months.



But the Blues prepared to cash in on him now, despite being one of the club's most consistent performers in a tough 2025/26 campaign.

Chalobah made 47 appearances in all competitions, and was ultimately rewarded with a late World Cup call-up for England.

He was a late replacement for Tino Livramento after the Newcastle man suffered a calf injury, and made his tournament debut in the Three Lions' crazy 6-4 third-place play-off win over France.

4 Chalobah would work under Fabregas should he move to Como Credit: Getty



Blues reunion?

Como are looking to strengthen by pulling off the signing of Chalobah's ahead of their first-ever Champions League campaign.

Under Fabregas, the Serie A outfit secured a fourth-place league finish last term to qualify for Europe for the first time.

And should they succeed in their pursuit of Chalobah, it would see him reunited with a familiar face in Fabregas.

The pair previously shared a dressing room at Chelsea, during the Spaniard's five-year stay in west London.



A Cobham academy graduate, Chalobah has been with the Blues since the age of eight.

He signed his first professional contract in March 2018 - while Fabregas was a key player for Chelsea.

4 Chalobah could be set to depart Chelsea after making 151 appearances for the club Credit: Getty

4 The defender has spent this summer as part of England's World Cup squad, following his late call-up Credit: Getty



Chalobah was named on the bench in the 2018 FA Cup final, when Chelsea beat Manchester United 1-0 at Wembley.

Fabregas played the full 90 minutes that day, but the two never shared the pitch together at Stamford Bridge.

The Spaniard has already managed to talk one of his old teammates into joining Como, with Alvaro Morata completing a permanent move after spending last season on loan in northern Italy.

And Chalobah has certainly managed to catch Fabregas' eye in the years since his departure from Chelsea in 2019.



After a series of loans in his early career, the centre-back has gone on to establish himself in the Blues backline in more recent seasons.

Last season was his best in west London, with his 47 appearances the most he has ever made in a single campaign for the club by some distance, while he also chipped in with two goals.

Sports.title: Arsenal exploring shock deal to sign Vinicius Jr after Premier League rivals decide against move
Sports.content:
Arsenal exploring shock deal to sign Vinicius Jr after Premier League rivals decide against move

Arsenal are contemplating a move for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior, talkSPORT understands.

The Gunners are yet to engage in club-to-club talks for the Brazilian, with the player viewed as an option rather than their number one target.

4 Vinicius Junior is on Arsenal's radar ahead of a possible summer switch Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old has also been offered to Liverpool, however the Reds have opted against pursuing the transfer.

Arsenal’s interest comes after Real Madrid tabled an offer for RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande.

The LaLiga giants saw an opening bid of £85.4million rejected by Leipzig.

However Madrid are confident of tying up a deal for the Ivory Coast international.

Gunner get ya?

Vinicius Jr and Diomande are part of the same agency meaning Diomande could be a direct replacement for the Brazilian.

It is also believed that Vinicius Jr's wages could prove to be stumbling block for the Premier League champions should they look to formalise their interest.

And there is currently no indication that Vini Jr will end up at the Emirates, despite being on Arsenal's radar.

Though they are prepared to open talks if they are given encouragement from the player.

Real Madrid are keen to not lose the forward on a free transfer with the winger tied down at the Bernabeu until 2027.

As of yet, there has been no breakthrough in terms of Vini Jr extending his stay.

4 The winger showed he has lost none of his shine in the World Cup Credit: Getty

4 Could the player end up at the Emirates this window?

Should Real fail to make progress on a deal then a move away form the club cannot be ruled out, according to sources at the Spanish club.

Renewal talks have taken place for over a year with an agreement having come close.

Vinicius Jr previously halted negotiations after falling out with former boss Xabi Alonso.

He has been linked with a money-spinning move to Saudi Arabia with Al Ahli with a €1bn five-year contract offered to him last year.

Brazil's talisman

The winger was arguably Brazil's standout player during the World Cup.

He featured in each of his country's five matches at the tournament, scoring four goals before their eventual round-of-16 defeat to Norway.

4 Vini Jr endured a frustrating season for Madrid but still posted 22 goals Credit: Getty

Last season, he netted 22 times in an underwhelming campaign for Real Madrid.

Los Blancos ended the season without silverware having finished runners-up to rivals Barcelona in La Liga.

But he has been embroiled in high-profile controversies during the course of the season including a racism storm in the Champions League clash against Benfica in February.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua fights back tears as he dedicates dramatic victory over Kristian Prenga to two best friends killed in car crash as he recovers from TWO knockdowns to win on return
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua fights back tears as he dedicates dramatic victory over Kristian Prenga to two best friends killed in car crash as he recovers from TWO knockdowns to win on return

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anthony Joshua knows better than anyone how quickly heavyweight boxing can tear up the script. And for a moment on Saturday night in Jeddah, it looked as though another shock was unfolding as the British heavyweight was dropped twice and wrestled to the canvas in a chaotic opening round.

But Joshua dug deep, weathered the storm and, after finding another gear in the second, produced a devastating combination that flattened Albanian heavyweight Kristian Prenga, leaving the 35-year-old sprawled on his back and bringing a dramatic end to a fight that had threatened to derail his comeback before it had even begun.

Although, when AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary.

For the first time since returning to the ring, the grief that he had worked so hard to suppress finally appeared.

The former two-time heavyweight world champion appeared, perhaps for the first time in public, to let the emotions he had buried since Latif 'Latz' Ayodele and Sina Ghami's tragic deaths in a car crash in Nigeria last December finally surface.

Joshua admitted before the fight that he had spent months suppressing the pain of losing the two men - Latz, his strength coach, and Sina, his personal trainer - insisting he did not want to make their deaths about himself while their families mourned.

Yet, after completing the hardest comeback of his career, both physically and mentally, the emotion could no longer be contained. Joshua broke down during his post-fight interview when crediting his friends for getting him through the first round before quietly saying: 'I don't want to talk about it anymore.'

Anthony Joshua gave an emotional interview after beating Kristian Prenga in Jeddah

When AJ's hand was raised, the victory itself almost felt secondary

Joshua was overcome with emotion after the fight, going from a euphoric high to an emotional low within minutes

For months after the crash, Joshua lived with constant pain. Simply getting out of bed became a struggle. He spent two months gently pedalling on a stationary bike before learning how to balance on a stability ball as he rebuilt his body from the ground up.

While the mental toll must have been every bit as demanding, if not more.

That said, Joshua and Eddie Hearn never liked calling this his 'comeback fight'. Seven months out of the ring is hardly unusual for a heavyweight. He had never truly been away from boxing.

But in every way that mattered, this was a comeback.

Because making it back into the ring after losing two of the people closest to him was perhaps Joshua’s greatest challenge of all.

There were moments when returning to the ring did not feel important, or even possible. But eventually, boxing became part of the healing process.

And so, under the bright lights of the Jeddah Superdome and with Latz and Sina embodied on the canvas, Joshua walked back into battle carrying far more than the pressure of victory on his shoulders.

Prenga was never supposed to be the final destination. The Albanian was always viewed as the bridge to something much bigger.

From the moment the fight was announced, it was understood that the real prize was Fury later this year.

This was the tune-up. The opportunity for Joshua to shake off the ring rust, rebuild momentum and remind the heavyweight division exactly who he is.

That is not to say there was no danger. There always is in the heavyweight division and Joshua was reminded of that the hard way.

Prenga entered the contest with 20 knockouts from 20 victories and just a single defeat. The power was genuine. In heavyweight boxing, one punch can change everything, and for a moment it looked as though it might.

The Albanian dominated a chaotic opening round, dropping Joshua twice and threatening to rip up the script.

Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round

But Joshua recovered in the second round, knocking Kristian Prenga out

It's anticipated that Joshua will finally fight Tyson Fury after both heavyweights won their fights this weekend

But there are levels in elite boxing. Prenga had never shared a ring with anyone approaching Joshua's pedigree or experience, and once the former two-time world champion returned to his corner and received a stern dressing down from his coaching team, he emerged with renewed purpose.

Still showing signs of the defensive vulnerabilities that have haunted him throughout his career, Joshua nevertheless displayed the resilience that has defined his comeback. He turned the tide in emphatic fashion, unleashing a devastating combination to stop Prenga 2:43 into the second round.

When Joshua's hand was raised, the emotion he had worked so hard to suppress could finally be contained no longer.

He had warned beforehand that he had kept so much inside. He did not want to centre himself in a story that belonged to grieving families. He wanted to honour his friends privately.

Instead, he pledged lifelong financial support to both families and vowed to continue pursuing the dreams they all shared together.

Yet as victory was confirmed in Jeddah, it was impossible not to think of everything he had endured to get there.

This was never just another win.

But there was one person missing: Tyson Fury.

Only 24 hours earlier, Fury had fought Mariusz Wach in Thailand, going seven rounds before the veteran Pole retired on his stool in a non-televised contest.

All week Fury had insisted he would not be travelling to Saudi Arabia for Joshua's fight and, despite widespread expectation that he would make a late appearance, the former world champion stayed away.

His absence did little to dampen the belief that British boxing's biggest fight is edging closer, but it denied fans the image they have waited years to see.

After so many failed negotiations, collapsed deals and false starts, supporters had hoped to see Joshua and Fury stand face-to-face in the ring for the first time with both men coming off victories.

But experience has taught Joshua not to assume anything in heavyweight boxing.

His long-awaited showdown with Deontay Wilder appeared all but set before Wilder suffered a shock defeat by Joseph Parker in December 2023 on the very same night Joshua won, sending months of planning into the bin.

The heavyweight division has a habit of snatching away the fights everyone wants to see.

Joshua wore a jacket featuring a medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua honoured his friends, Latz and Sina, who were killed in a car crash in December

That is why there will remain a degree of caution until the AJ vs Fury fight is officially confirmed.

Joshua and Eddie Hearn have already revealed that the contract stipulates any showdown with Fury must take place in the United Kingdom because, in their eyes, the biggest fight in British boxing history belongs on British soil.

As things stand, however, Turki Alalshikh and Netflix are understood to favour Madison Square Garden in New York.

That means the contracts will need to be renegotiated.

The expectation is that discussions between all parties will take place over the coming days as they attempt to iron out the remaining details.

For now, Joshua's focus was not on what comes next, but on what he had already overcome.

The tears in Jeddah were not for Tyson Fury.

They were for Latz and Sina.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty kisses pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he misses out on gold and finishes in third place in the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty kissed pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he missed out on his 33rd major gold medal as he finished in third place in the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday.

The 18-year-old from Jersey Filip Nowacki finished ahead of his idol in second, but gold went to Australian Sam Williamson.

Williamson finished in 59.17 seconds, while Nowacki was milliseconds behind at 59.34 and Ramsay-Peaty behind him at 59.65.

Despite her husband missing out on the gold, Holly was ever the proud wife as she packed on the PDA with Adam after the medal ceremony.

The swimmer sweetly kissed his wife's growing baby bump before breaking down in tears over his 'hurtful' loss.

He said: 'I'm never afraid to show emotion. It's important because it helps create stronger people, stronger men, stronger fathers and stronger husbands.

'This cycle especially, I've worked harder than ever. To get a result like that hurts because I know I'm better than that.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty kissed pregnant wife Holly's baby bump as he finished in third place in 100m breaststroke final at Commonwealth Games on Saturday

The couple packed on the PDA after the swimmer missed out on his 33rd major gold medal

Adam was the favourite to win the 100m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games but only managed to secure third place

'It's still very raw. I honestly feel like I deserve more. There's a lot of thinking to do, but it's too early to draw any conclusions.

'Maybe it was just an off swim. Maybe it's because I've been away from championship racing for two years. I honestly don't know.

'What's the point of all the 5.30am starts? What's the point of all the metres every single day? What's the point of being exhausted all the time, or missing family events because you have to train?

'It has to mean something. For me, that means striving for excellence, and today wasn't excellence. That's where the emotion comes from.

'The choices I've made over the last few months have been difficult. At the same time, I'm proud that I got here and that I didn't quit after Paris [Olympics]. I know I deserve more, and I know I can work for it.

'It's been two years since I've raced heats, semis and finals, so maybe it's just an adjustment. It's too early to know what I'm capable of at this stage, but I'm a fighter.

'We've got another opportunity at the Europeans in two weeks, and I do enjoy a scrap. I lost that scrap today, but that's sport. Most of the time I've won those battles – this time I didn't.'

However, reports of his strained relationship with his parents have clearly taken their toll on Adam, as he added that he can't continue.

He continued: 'Over the last couple of months I've had to make some hard decisions so I could focus on doing my job.

'I've had to ignore a lot of the rubbish people write online. Enough is enough. This goes beyond sport. It's about being decent people. We all have to do better.

'My wife will always be proud of me. As a father, it doesn't matter whether you come home with a gold medal, as long as you come home. That's what really matters.'

Ahead of the Games, Holly, who announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam, couldn't contain her smile as she took her seat to watch her husband, 31, compete in the final.

Holly, who is the daughter of TV chef Gordon Ramsay, 26, showed off her blossoming baby bump in a simple black T-shirt and matching jumper.

His pregnant Holly Ramsay couldn't contain her smile as she arrived to watch husband Adam compete in the final

Following the race, Adam admitted he was disappointed in his result: 'I've worked harder than ever. To get a result like that hurts because I know I'm better than that. It's still very raw'

Holly looked so proud of her husband after the race

Holly showed off her blossoming baby bump in a simple black T-shirt and matching jumper as she showed her support to Adam

The couple hugged after the tense final

The couple packed on the PDA after the race

Adam sweetly kissed Holly's baby bump

The couple looked more loved-up than ever after tying the knot in December

Adam was seen getting ready for the final

During the heats on Friday, Adam won despite a 10-minute delay caused by a detached lane rope.

He posted the fastest qualifying time and advanced comfortably to the semifinals and then progressed through the semifinals to book his place in the final.

The three-time Olympic champion is taking part in his fourth Commonwealth Games having clinched his first medals as a 19-year-old in Glasgow in 2014.

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

Adam told TNT Sports: 'Job done, really. We've got a busy two weeks coming up, so we're reserving energy where we can.

'Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it's been a very long journey.'

Ramsay-Peaty debuted his new name on his swimming cap at the Commonwealth Games as he hopes his new moniker will bring him luck.

The three-time Olympic swimming champion is using his full name for the first time to compete at a major championship after marrying TV chef Gordon Ramsay's daughter Holly last December.

Sadly his parents did not attend the wedding and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them.

Join the discussion Should family come before sporting fame, even if it risks your career?

The daughter of TV chef Gordon Ramsay, 26, looked excited as she took her seat in the crowd to watch her partner, 31

Styling her dark tresses loose, the star wore a radiant palette of makeup and accessorised with a simple cross necklace

The pregnant influencer was spotted staying hydrated in the crowd ahead of Adam competing in the final after he won his heat on Saturday

Holly cheered on Adam from the crowd

Holly was all smiles as she chatted with friends in the stands

The 18-year-old from Jersey Filip Nowacki finished ahead of his idol in second, but gold went to Australian Sam Williamson

Adam debuted his new name Ramsay-Peaty on his swimming cap at the Commonwealth Games as he hopes his new moniker will bring him luck

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail revealed that Adam's pregnant sister Bethany – the only member of his family to still be in contact with the couple – has now sensationally fallen out with Holly.

Not only are they no longer communicating, but this time it is Adam who is stuck in the middle, trying (and so far failing) to mend fences. Read the full story here.

The roots of the family conflict go back to September 2024, when Adam and Holly snubbed wider members of the Peaty family by not inviting them to their engagement party.

Caroline, who spent years ferrying her son to early-morning training sessions, was also not invited to Holly's glamorous hen do at Soho Farmhouse in the Cotswolds, even though the bride's mother, Tana, and friends including Victoria, were at the extravagant bash.

Adam changing his name to Ramsay-Peaty and registering under the double-barrel surname for the Games in Glasgow is the latest blow for his estranged loved ones – especially as Ramsay is placed first before Peaty.

A source said previously: 'Adam may be rich but we have something that he hasn't and that is brains, loyalty, integrity and family.

'Money makes for a cold bedfellow. It can't hold you tight when things go wrong or when you have a bad day.'

They added: 'When you live to be famous you aren't living, you are playing a role. Fame is but fleeting but family is forever.'

Adam's heat was temporarily halted as he was on the blocks when a lane divider broke off, requiring an official to strip to the waist and enter the pool to reconnect it.

The athlete duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds, with only two rivals, Australia's Sam Williamson and Filip Nowacki of Jersey, also finishing in under a minute.

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

The influencer announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua pays tribute to his two best friends killed in a car crash as he returns to the ring for clash with Kristian Prenga
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua paid tribute to two close friends killed in a car crash in December as he returned to the ring for the first time since the tragedy.

Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele died while the car they were travelling in struck a truck on a road near Lagos in December. The pair were on holiday with Joshua after he beat Jake Paul in Miami.

The heavyweight boxer, who was also in the vehicle, was taken to hospital before being discharged and flying home to the UK - where he attended the funerals of his strength and conditioning coach Ghami and Ayodele, one of his trainers.

Returning to the ring after seven months of inactivity, Joshua beat Albanian Kristian Prenga by knockout in the second round - despite being knocked down twice himself in the first.

Fighting in honour of Ghami and Ayodele, Joshua paid tribute to his friends by having their names printed on his military camouflage trunks.

He also walked to the ring wearing a military-style jacket to match his camo shorts. The jacket featured a medal bar displaying the IBF, IBO, WBA, and WBO titles - which he previously held - alongside pennants bearing Ghami and Ayodele's names.

Meanwhile, ‘Latz x Sina, My Brother's Keeper, MBK’ was printed on the canvas in his corner.

Anthony Joshua wears jacket featuring medal bar with 'Sina' and 'Latz' pennants

Joshua's friends were honoured by having their names printed on the canvas

Asked about how he has been coping after beating Prenga, Joshua said: 'It's been tough,' before becoming emotional. 'That's my brothers. I don't want to talk about that.'

Speaking on DAZN, Matchroom Boxing chief Eddie Hearn added: 'Nobody can imagine what he's been through in that last seven months. In that first round, I thought we'd come back too soon.

'Boxing got him through. To even be in the ring tonight is astonishing. You don't know what he's been through. He had to go to the depths one more time to get up, like he has done the last seven months.'

In February, Joshua memorialised Ghami and Ayodele by having their names tattooed on his arm.

Oleksandr Usyk was ringside for the clash in Jeddah to support Joshua, whom he beat twice in world title fights. Usyk has been working closely with Joshua, supporting his training camp.

Victory for Joshua means he is on track to finally fight Tyson Fury in a long-awaited British heavyweight showdown.

Sports.title: 'Hurt' Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after surprise Commonwealth Games bronze: Star reveals family feud has taken its toll and admits he 'doesn't know what went wrong'
Sports.content:
First came an apology. 'Sorry guys,' said Adam Ramsay-Peaty, as his voice began to tremble. He wiped away a tear from his face and stared at the Tollcross floor to find his words.

The bronze medal around his neck felt like a heavy weight. 'It's hard because I know how hard I've worked. I know the s**t I've been through, which is no fault of my own. It does take a toll.'

After standing upon the podium, the 31-year-old walked around the pool and stopped for selfies with his adoring fans. An Englishman has not received a reception like this in Glasgow for a long time.

He stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly – the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay – before kissing her pregnant stomach. They are expecting a daughter in December and, as the swimmer confessed, family life has changed his priorities.

'She's always super proud of me,' he said. 'As a father, it doesn't matter if you come home with the gold, as long as you come home with the teddy, which I did. That's what matters.

'As you can tell, the emotion is always something that I'm going to carry. I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness because it's so important for making stronger people, making stronger men, stronger fathers, stronger husbands.

'I think 'S**t, how have I worked so hard at this age?' - then you get a result like that. I'm better than that. Maybe it's because I've had two years out, but it does hurt. There's a lot going on in my head right now.'

Adam Ramsay-Peaty was brought to tears as he reflected 'I'm never going to be afraid to show weakness' after securing bronze at the Commonwealth games

Adam Ramsay-Peaty stopped to hug his pregnant wife, Holly - the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay - before kissing her pregnant stomach

The pair wed on December 27 last year at Bath Abbey

Ramsay-Peaty was chasing from the start. He was not the leader of the pack. Perhaps he will fare better over 50 metres but here, over two lengths, he finished almost three seconds off his world record.

Australian Sam Williamson won gold and 18-year-old Filip Nowacki, of Jersey, claimed a brilliant silver that bodes well for the future of British swimming.

'I'm not crying because it's a bronze instead of a gold,' said Peaty, choking up throughout. 'I'm crying because I know that swim could have been better. I don't really know what went wrong in these last two weeks but something isn't hitting right, whether it's pace or focus.

'I feel like I couldn't have put more in, so you ask, 'What's the point of all the 5.30ams. What's the point of all the metres every day? What's the point of feeling exhausted all the time? What's the point of saying, 'No' to all the family events because of training?' It's because you want excellence and that isn't excellence for me.

'I enjoy a scrap but I lost that scrap in the last 25 metres. That's sport. Most of the time I've won the scrap. For some reason, the Commonwealths is that humble reminder.'

The wedding stories, the family feud and the social media abuse have taken their toll. The pool should be his place of escape but he swam with the world on his shoulders.

'People who comment and read headlines have got to look themselves in the mirror. Ignoring that comes at a cost. That hasn't played a part in that result here but it has to stop. Do better. I don't want young Filip to go through that.'

Ramsay-Peaty was overcome with emotion in the mixed zone reflecting on his bronze medal

Throughout his decorated career, Ramsay-Peaty has been so far ahead of the field that he has had to look in the mirror to find competition. He has broken 14 world records, asserting a similar dominance to Sweden's serial pole vault champion Armand Duplantis. Untouchables. Now people will ask if time is finally catching up with Britain's greatest swimmer.

Nowacki is still waiting for his A Level results but the schoolboy from Millfield has already beaten his idol's teenage records. In 2012, Jason Kenny beat Chris Hoy to become the top dog of cycling. Lamine Yamal overcame Lionel Messi in last week's World Cup final. Swimming insiders believe it is a matter of time until Nowacki pulls a similar stunt.

'For me, he's got a very bright future ahead of him,' said Ramsay-Peaty, whose gold earrings caught the light of the cameras. 'He's my favourite for the 200m. He's definitely got the speed and he's about 25kgs less! He's got many many miles ahead of him, whereas my miles are probably coming to an end. I guess two years isn't that long to try and find that in me.'

Side by side, they look like David and Goliath. Nowacki is five inches shorter and does not have the same popping biceps. Ramsay-Peaty changed the game with his powerful upper body stroke but Nowacki's strength is in his kick. He keeps his hips high and moves more gracefully than his senior, who forces his way through the water.

Nowacki will discover his maths, economics and physics exam results during next month's European Championships. Then he plans to enrol at Loughborough University, where he can master his craft in time for the LA 2028 Olympics. Major medals are in his sights, although Ramsay-Peaty is not ready to stand aside just yet.

'To be racing one of the best in the world – arguably the greatest breaststroker of all time – is very special to me,' said Nowacki, who won the world junior championships last year in a time of 2:07.32, which would have medalled in every senior Olympics, bar one

Ramsay-Peaty knows a promising swimmer when he sees one. He has already signed up Nowacki to his own agency and will continue to mentor his prodigy.

'If I compare myself to 2014, 12 years ago, it's very exciting where Filip and his career can go,' he said. 'It's sport, it's beautiful, but f**k me, it can hurt.'

Sports.title: Sole British contender Kalpana stuns favourite to surge to impressive victory in King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Ascot
Sports.content:
Sole British contender Kalpana saw off a stellar international field to hand trainer Andrew Balding an emotional first victory in the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes.

Ascot's Group One showpiece has been synonymous with the Balding family since Andrew's late father, Ian, won it with his legendary Derby winner Mill Reef in 1971.

'It is a big deal as it is a race we have always wanted to win,' said a visibly emotional Balding, who sent out a rapid Group race treble in the space of two hours — thanks to Moonrise's success in the Princess Margaret Stakes earlier on the card and Item's Group Two win at York.

'It defines a season, and it defines a career a race like this. I'm so pleased.'

Referring to his family's legacy with the race, Balding added: 'We have grown up with it. I think the first ever winner of the race was trained at Kingsclere [where Balding trains], it is lovely to bring it back all these years later.'

For his part, jockey Colin Keane was a little more measured, saying: 'I'm just delighted for the filly. Although she's won two Group Ones, she probably deserves to have won a couple more and she showed her true class today.

'It was one of the strongest renewals of the race, with horses coming from all over the globe, so for her to go and do it today is very special.'

Kalpana saw off a stellar international field to hand trainer Andrew Balding an emotional first victory

In a race run at a furious gallop, courtesy of two Ballydoyle pacemakers, Mickael Barzalona adopted patient tactics aboard reigning champion Calandagan before attempting to reel in Kalpana from the two-furlong marker.

However, in contrast to 12 months ago, the 6-5 favourite could not overhaul Balding's mare who kept on powerfully to score by a cosy length and a half, with Irish Derby winner Benvenuto Cellini a creditable third.

While disappointed at his gelding's defeat, Calandagan's trainer, Francis-Henri Graffard, was content with the performance.

'This season hasn't been as smooth as last year,' Graffard said.

'Epsom [Calandagan finished fourth in the Coronation Cup] was a disaster and then, Saint-Cloud, he won a good race there but they had changed the date of the race and it was much closer to this race.

'So, it gave me less time to get him very fresh for today and, also, it's a heatwave in France — it takes a lot of energy of the horses. So with all these factors he still ran a very good race.'

Master trainer Aidan O'Brien was also content with the efforts of Benvenuto Cellini, who saw out the 1m 4f trip well.

He said: 'I was very happy with Benvenuto Cellini. He ran a great race. It was his first time against the older horses, and we learnt a lot about him.

'We learnt he gets the mile and a half well, and you couldn't be sure of that until he did it against the older horses. Even going to the line he didn't looked finished.

'I think we could look at the Breeders' Cup.'

Unfortunately, there were few positives in the performances of Japanese contenders Masquerade Ball and Wurttemberg, who never figured in seventh and ninth respectively.

Away from the big race here on a sunny Berkshire afternoon, Saffie Osborne rode a sparkling 274-1 treble, with superb victories aboard Amazing Journey and Hickory, for her father Jamie, and Primo Lara for trainer Jane Chapple-Hyam.

'I love Ascot and it has been very lucky for me, with the exception of the Royal meeting,' enthused the thrilled rider. 'All three horses

had a chance but it would have been a bit adventurous to think they would all win. It's very special.'

Chapple-Hyam enjoyed two winners herself at the track yesterday, with the Ryan Moore-ridden Kon Tiki impressively capturing the Group Three Valiant Stakes to supplement Primo Lara's later victory.

Sports.title: The ultimate football bromance reunited as Morgan Rogers seals £117m move to Chelsea: England star and Cole Palmer share a celebration, grew up together at Man City and are linked by a tragic bond
Sports.content:
Monday, November 2, 2020. St George’s Park, Burton-on-Trent. The FA Youth Cup final between Manchester City and Chelsea. It is 2-2 as we approach the 83rd minute. Morgan Rogers has already scored for City, a tidy finish to a low cross cut back by Liam Delap.

Then Delap breaks behind. He shoots. The ball bobbles beyond Chelsea defender Levi Colwill and trickles towards the back post, where Cole Palmer is waiting. He taps in for 3-2 and that’s that at the FA’s national football centre. City win, Chelsea lose.

Those in attendance might never have guessed what a Chelsea connection this youth match involving City would carry nearly six years later, now that Rogers is signing for £117million, the most expensive fee ever paid for a British player.

Both 18 years old at the time, neither Rogers nor Palmer performed their now customary ‘Cold’ celebrations after scoring. That trademark came later in their careers.

Instead, when Palmer grabbed the winner for Carlos Vicens’ academy class of 2020 at City, he lifted his shirt to reveal a tribute to Jeremy Wisten, his former team-mate who had died by suicide just nine days before.

Young footballers form bonds when they dream of making it big together, and we will never know what might have become of Wisten, a teenager who wrestled with his release by City. It was a poignant gesture by Palmer to reveal a ‘GBNF’ (‘Gone But Never Forgotten’) undershirt so that his late friend was involved in their first FA Youth Cup triumph since 2008.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have been friends and team-mates since their days in Man City's academy

The pair share a celebration but Rogers' £117m move to Chelsea will also see them share the pitch for the first time in nearly six years

Watching back this final, it is striking how all three of City’s goals involved a player now owned by Chelsea. For their first, Delap occupied Chelsea’s centre backs as Palmer squeezed a pass by Colwill for the unmarked James McAtee to finish.

For their second, Colwill was marking Palmer as Delap crossed and Rogers scored.

For their third, Delap’s saved shot crept to Palmer to complete the 3-2 scoreline, with Colwill smashing the ball into the back of the net in frustration while City celebrated. Now they are all set to be team-mates at Stamford Bridge moving forward in a case of graduates reunited. Once City’s next generation. Suddenly Chelsea’s future.

With Rogers and Palmer in particular, this £117m move from Aston Villa rekindles a friendship, it being no secret that the two are close. They have described each other as best friends in football. They are on WhatsApp and FaceTime almost daily, as we all are with our own pals. Both believed in what the other was capable of achieving back when they were with City, and so for them personally, it is rather nice that they are teaming up again at Chelsea.

While away with England, Rogers’ team-mates liked jesting on the ownership of his celebration. Jude Bellingham was asked during one interview whose was better: his or Rogers’. Sitting next to Rogers, Bellingham pondered and said: ‘Mine or Cole’s?’ Chelsea’s content team will be buzzing with ideas for how they can play on this ‘Cold’ competition.

Rogers did it first while playing for Middlesbrough, but technically, Palmer owns it. He has it trademarked with the UK Intellectual Property Office for commercial reasons. It entered the register in November 2025, and is not due for renewal until November 2034.

Palmer debuted it in a 3-2 win away at Luton in December 2023 and has since told reporters that he did it as ‘a nod’ to Rogers. They’re mates, so Rogers does not mind too much that he pinched it from him. From Chelsea's perspective, they will hope they can score enough goals between them to take turns and share it amicably.

Palmer may have seen this move coming. Before the end of the last season, several Chelsea players held talks with the club’s owners and directors, Palmer included. It was at a time when he was being linked to Manchester United despite Chelsea sources tagging him as one of their untouchable assets. Assurances were made, and also to Reece James when the captain signed his new contract through to 2032. Palmer spoke at length with James about what he was told.

Chelsea has kept a close eye on Rogers since he was at Middlesborough (pictured in 2024)

Palmer celebrated his friend's signing with a touching Instagram post documenting their bond

Chelsea promised they were now going to recruit ‘ready-made’ signings this summer. Missing out on Champions League football – or any form of European qualification for that matter – was a complication. But they have spent big to beat Arsenal to the signing of Rogers. He meets that ‘ready-made’ criteria. James is said to have been pleading his club’s case while they were both away at this summer's World Cup.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso had his first behind-closed-doors friendly at the weekend, with Daily Mail Sport revealing the scoreline was 3-1 and the scorers were Delap, Jamie Gittens and Emmanuel Emegha. One source also told us they used a 4-2-3-1 formation. One solution would be Palmer at No 10 and Rogers on the left, or Rogers at No 10 and Palmer on the right. If Alonso uses a 3-4-2-1, both could feature behind Joao Pedro as the starting striker.

Their versatility gives Alonso options, and while Rogers has been a long-term target for Chelsea, the 44-year-old Spaniard very much sanctioned this transfer after arriving. We can sometimes suspect it is hot air when a new manager is telling us how he is on the same page as those above him, but in this particular case, it is true.

Rogers will be due some downtime after his World Cup exploits with England, three weeks being the usual break. That means he may miss their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia. Whenever he rocks up, coldness could ensue. Certainly, after spending £117m to bring the boys back together, Chelsea hope it will be positively Siberian.

Man United goalkeeper emerges as target for Championship side, Spurs push for City star Savinho and Chelsea REJECT Como bid for Trevoh Chalobah: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Real Madrid's play for £100m man Yan Diomande - click HERE

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Boro after United goalkeeper

Manchester United goalkeeper Radek Vitek has emerged as a target for Middlesbrough.

Several Championship clubs have asked for a loan of the Czech while Premier League sides have also enquired, with Hull City among them.

The 22-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Bristol City, is among a number of options Boro are looking at.

United also expect to sell Altay Bayindir this summer.

Spurs push for Savinho

Tottenham are continuing their pursuit of Manchester City winger Savinho.

Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi says they need to sign another two attacking players this summer.

The North London club have already spent £237m on six new signings and De Zerbi wants more.

'The target now is to complete the attacking positions,' he said.

'I think to start the new project we need another couple of important players, for sure. It's not finished yet.'

Como see Chalobah bid rejected

Chelsea have rejected Como's latest offer for Trevoh Chalobah.

The two clubs met on Saturday for talks over the 27-year-old. However, Como offered a package worth £25.6million which is still short of Chelsea's valuation of £30m plus add-ons.

Como are now considering other options.

Chalobah also had interest from Inter Milan and Crystal Palace this summer but they are working on other targets.

He has two years left on his contract, plus a club-held option for a third.

Belgian side monitoring City youngster

The 20-year-old has had varying degrees of success on loan at PSV Eindhoven, Nottingham Forest, Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday over the past two years.

City paid Port Vale £300,000 to bring Ndala to the club in 2017.

Gunners eye ambitious Vini swoop

Arsenal have made initial enquiries over the availability of Real Madrid winger Vini Jr.

With Jose Mourinho's side exploring the purchase of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, the Premier League champions have checked on the Brazilian's status as speculation grows over where his future lies.

The 26-year-old has the same representatives as Diomande, who was also on Arsenal's radar, and there has been interest from Saudi Arabi over the past 12 months.

The deal would represent a sensational coup for Arsenal if they were successful but the clubs are still to open official talks.

Forest table fresh bid for Feyenoord star

Nottingham Forest have submitted an improved £17.5million bid for Feyenoord right-back Givairo Read.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month how Forest had targeted the highly-rated 20-year-old defender who has also been in Manchester City's radar.

Forest are working on a £35m deal for Sporting Lisbon centre-back Ousmane Diomande and are also weighing a move for Everton striker Beto.

They are expected to place a new £45m bid for Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall.

Nottingham Forest have submitted an improved £17.5million bid for Feyenoord's Givairo Read

Celtic on brink of club record move

Celtic are closing on a club record £11million deal for Bodo/Glimt striker Kasper Hogh.

The Denmark international is due to arrive tonight for a medical ahead of agreeing a four-year contract, with Celtic having the option to extend by a further year.

Hogh was a target for Norwich City in January and had an impressive Champions League campaign.

Hammers reject Diouf approach

Sports.title: Inside LeBron James's family feud with new Philadelphia 76ers teammate amid the bombshell move that rocked the NBA
Sports.content:
LeBron James sent shockwaves through the NBA on Friday when he announced the final stop in his remarkable career would be with the Philadelphia 76ers.

The 41-year-old, who left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons, admitted he thought he had played his final game in the NBA, but has decided instead to sign a two-year deal – worth around $8 million – with the Sixers.

But he did so without any guarantee he would walk into a welcoming environment. Yes, the pieces seem to be in place in America's birthplace for instant success, but talks were needed 'to clear the air' before their superstar's arrival.

There would have definitely been an awkward reunion with Jaylen Brown, whose trade from the Boston Celtics to Philadelphia earlier in the offseason is believed to have been a major factor in the recruitment of James.

While with the Celtics, Brown went viral for some unflattering comments he made about James' son, Bronny, after he was drafted by his dad's Lakers back in 2024.

In a blunt assessment of the then-rookie's ability, Brown said: 'I don't think Bronny is a pro.' Brown also rattled the cage of another new teammate, Joel Embiid, earlier this year.

LeBron James, pictured with wife Savannah, stunned the NBA by signing with the Sixers

After being eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the Sixers, Brown said: 'Flopping has ruined our league. Joel Embiid is one of the greatest players that has played basketball, but he flops. He knows it too.'

But The Daily Mail understands Sixers executives have been trying to smooth things over behind the scenes in recent weeks. Honest discussions have taken place and the team's stars have buried the hatchet ahead of James' arrival.

A source told us: 'Any issues LeBron may have had with Jaylen (Brown) ultimately took a backseat because winning changes everything. The opportunity to join what the Sixers could become was simply too good to pass up.

'He's already won championships by changing teams in Miami and Cleveland, so returning to either situation would have felt like a step backward.

'And while Golden State had been viewed as the frontrunner for a while, it increasingly looked like more of a retirement tour than a true championship destination, especially with how difficult the path to the NBA Finals is in the Western Conference.

'The Eastern Conference presents a much more realistic road back to the Finals, particularly with the talent Philadelphia already has in place.'

They continued: 'Jaylen also had past issues with Joel Embiid, but conversations have been had, everything has been smoothed over. Tyrese Maxey's presence - along with his connection with Rich Paul - helped reassure everyone involved.

'In the end, it became the obvious choice. Everyone spoke with LeBron, cleared the air and made sure there would be no lingering problems.'

One of James' new teammates is Jaylen Brown, who questioned his son Bronny's ability

Brown's blockbuster trade from the Celtics is believed to have been key in recruiting James

It remains to be seen what James' wife, Savannah, will do. After eight years in Los Angeles and the glamorous lifestyle that comes with it, it is unclear how she feels about the prospect of returning to the East Coast.

Like her husband, Savannah was born in Akron, Ohio and the pair met when James was playing high school football and she was cheerleading for the rival team.

They share three children - Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri - but our source says James has made a promise to them that this will be his final shot at an elusive fifth NBA championship.

They added: 'Just as importantly, his wife and kids fully supported the move after LeBron assured them that this would be his final chapter. Once this is over, he's done.'

The NBA's all-time leading scorer made the announcement on social media Friday, saying it will be his 'last decision' and that it comes after he strongly considered retirement.

The Sixers, who went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round by the NBA champion New York Knicks and have not won an NBA championship since 1983, quickly emerged as favourites to win the championship with most betting sites.

'I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time,' James said.

A four-time NBA champion, James wrote he was 'done' when his 23rd NBA season ended and that it was his last with the Lakers.

'I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love this game,' James wrote. 'I still truly love this game, and I have more to give.'

Joel Embiid (right) also had issues with Brown but the team is focused on winning with James

Our source has said LeBron has promised his family this will be his final contract in the NBA

The 41-year-old James is set to sign a modest $8-million, two-year contract with the Sixers, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

'I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family,' James wrote. 'What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning.'

James celebrated his decision on Instagram with a career highlight reel set to Philadelphia rapper Meek Mill's 'Dreams and Nightmares,' the adopted sports anthem of city sports teams.

The video ends with the lyric, 'hold up, wait a minute. Y'all thought I was finished?' and cuts to a Sixers' logo. Philadelphia will be praying he can deliver one final special run.

Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua immediately told he’s “shot to bits” after KO win

Joshua scored a destructive knockout on his return to the ring on Saturday night to set up a fight with Tyson Fury - but not everyone was pleased with his performance

View Image Anthony Joshua celebrates victory over Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua has been brutally told he is 'shot to bits' just seconds after rendering Kristian Prenga unconscious on his return to the ring.

‌



The 36-year-old watched long-time rival Tyson Fury win on Friday night, and had to follow it up with a victory himself on Saturday night to make their highly-anticipated all-British showdown official. But he nearly saw the fight fall apart after he was dropped just seconds into the opening round by Prenga.

‌



A stunned Joshua looked all over the place in the early exchanges of the opening stanza, and nearly fell to the canvas for a second time, but was eventually saved by the bell. Prenga allowed Joshua to take control of the second round, and was made to pay when 'AJ' went in for the knockout.

‌



Joshua sent his Albanian rival crashing to the canvas with a destructive left hand, securing an inspiring win Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. But not everyone was convinced. Boxing coach Dave Coldwell offered a rather brutal take on the fight, posting: "Joshua is without a doubt shot to bits. Punch resistance looks completely gone. Last thing a fighter loses is his punch and that’s what got him out of jail tonight."

He added: "He's a strong guy and I think Eddie Hearn wants to sign him now! He is going to do well. He has a serious future. With experience he will be up there with the rest of us. He is strong, durable and have me a good test - but champions rise."

But all the talk coming into the fight was whether Fury would be ringside. Immediately after his win over Mariusz Wach, he hinted that he would make the trip to Saudi Arabia. But fans were left confused when Fury's security showed up to Jeddah on Saturday night without the 'Gypsy King.'

Fair do’s. Imma rip his heart out. I'm the meanest and vicious champion's ever been," he said.

Anthony Joshua sends violent message to Tyson Fury after brutal comeback KO

The former two-time heavyweight world champion was quick to send a warning to his long-time rival just moments after winning his comeback fight

Anthony Joshua has vowed to 'rip' Tyson Fury's heart out after sending a violent message to his rival just moments after knocking out Kristian Prenga.

The former two-time heavyweight champion returned to the ring on Saturday night - just months after escaping death after he was involved in a horrific car crash over in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

In the build up to fight week, there was a lot of talk about a potential clash between Fury and Joshua. Fury returned to the squared-circle on Friday night and forced veteran Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool at the end of the seventh to uphold his end of the bargain.

Joshua, on the other hand, nearly saw a fight with Fury fall apart after he was sent crashing to the canvas just seconds into his clash with Prenga. The Brit managed to climb back up, but nearly fell to the floor again. He clung on and made it to the second when he took the fight to Prenga before knocking out the Albanian.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua survives knockdowns to KO Kristian Prenga in Tyson Fury warm-up
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua survives knockdowns to KO Kristian Prenga in Tyson Fury warm-up

Anthony Joshua had to win to set up an all-British showdown with Tyson Fury but gave his fans a huge scare

View 4 Images Anthony Joshua was knocked down

Anthony Joshua recovered from two knockdowns in the first round to KO Kristian Prenga and set up a huge fight with Tyson Fury.

‌



Joshua was dropped seconds into what was supposed to be a routine warm-up fight and looked at one stage as if he would be stopped when he touched the canvas again. But he clung on to reach the second round when he took the fight to Prenga and stopped the Albanian.

‌



Joshua was fighting for the first time since he escaped death in a car crash last December and he ensured the names of his two friends who died in the smash were remembered by sewing their names into the canvas in front of his red corner.

‌



But disaster struck inside seconds as Joshua hit the canvas. He gave a wry smile as he picked himself up but he was in trouble again when Prenga pinned him to the ropes. And he was counted again with 30 seconds of the round remaining when he touched the floor - but he clung on to hear the bell.

View 4 Images Joshua was sent crashing to the canvas just seconds into the opening stanza but was able to hold on (Image: Getty Images)

Joshua began the second round with far more authority and with Prenga back-pedalling, the Brit landed a huge right hand which left the Albanian crumpled. Asked about fighting Fury, who failed to show up at ringside, Joshua said: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

‌



"All jokes aside, there are two sides to this thing. You have to have that vim as a fighter but also respect. I respect everything he has done and achieved but as a someone who has been calling for this fight for some time, it is here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

View 4 Images Joshua held on before brutally knocking Prenga out in the second (Image: Getty Images)

Earlier, Josh Kelly defended his super-welterweight world title with a thrilling points win over Caoimhin Agyarko. Kelly won his belt from the dangerous Bakhram Murtazaliev earlier this year and opted to put it on the line against Belfast's Agyarko. The Sunderland man dominated the contest from the opening bell, putting his challenger on the backfoot over the opening three rounds.

Agyarko was far more comfortable on the front foot by the sixth session and a left hand landed flush. Kelly was then deducted a point for punching to the back of the head having already been warned. The challenger was in the ascendency heading into the second half and another right hand found its mark - but Kelly landed successive left hands in response.

‌



View 4 Images Joshua celebrates win over Prenga (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Kelly began to breathe more heavily by the eighth round as a cut opened up on his right cheek. The champion was let off for a blatant low blow in the ninth round and right and left hands in the final minute of the session nicked him the round. Kelly summoned his reserves in the penultimate round and landed a right hand flush which Agyarko took well. Kelly's face was crimson and he was caught by a left as his challenger looked to seize his chance. The same shot in the dying seconds stole the round. Sports.title: British Paralympics medallist insists 'I never cheated' after receiving brutal two-year ban
Sports.content:
British Paralympics medallist insists 'I never cheated' after receiving brutal two-year ban

Paralympic cyclist Daphne Schrager was banned for two years after failing a drugs test

View 2 Images Daphne Schrager (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

British Paralympic medalist Daphne Schrager has stated that she has “never cheated” after she was handed a two-year ban for failing a drugs test. Schrager, a para-cyclist, won a silver medal for Great Britain during the 2024 Paralympics in Paris.

‌



An out-of-competition drug test in April 2025 found that Schrager had tested positive for Ligandrol, a substance on the banned list that can increase muscle and bone mass.

‌



Schrager, who is from Malmesbury, has made it clear that she has never used banned substances and argued that exposure through environmental contamination was the reason for the positive test.

‌



Two potential scenarios were presented, including a massage she had received at a gym, or at a shared residential address.

However, a National Anti-Doping Panel tribunal determined that while Schrager had not deliberately used a banned substance, she had not demonstrated that it was an accidental environmental contamination.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Consequently, the 25-year-old was issued a two-year ban from competition, which has been backdated to commence from the date of her initial suspension on June 2, 2025, and will conclude on June 1, 2027.

The two-year rather than the four-year ban does leave the possibility open for Schrager to potentially participate at the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. In a lengthy statement posted on Instagram, Schrager revealed she had commissioned hair and nail analysis in an attempt to prove her innocence - yet as the precise origin of the contamination could not be pinpointed, the ban was upheld.

"In June last year, I received news that turned my world upside down," she said. "I had tested positive in an anti-doping test for a trace amount of Ligandrol, detected at 0.0006ng, resulting in my suspension from cycling since that time.

‌



"I want to be very clear: I have never cheated, nor have I ever knowingly taken any banned substance. Facing the possibility of a four-year ban unless I could prove that the result was unintentional has been incredibly distressing."

The tribunal was told that Schrager firmly denied ever using prohibited substances and maintained that she had never deliberately breached the ADR.

She provided testimony that the presence of Ligandrol was the result of environmental contamination rather than deliberate use, either through exposure at the gym she visited two days prior to her sample being collected, or alternatively, through environmental contamination within her shared home.

‌



View 2 Images Daphne Schrager (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

The Tribunal considered scientific evidence from a number of experts, alongside additional testimony. The experts were in agreement that inadvertent environmental contamination was responsible for the positive test, concluding that Schrager had not intentionally used Ligandrol.

The Tribunal was also convinced, on the balance of probabilities, that there was no recklessness in Schrager's attendance at the gym, but they observed that as Schrager had not established how Ligandrol entered her system, she had unintentionally committed anti-doping offences and thus imposed her two-year period of ineligibility.

‌



"In cases like mine, by the time an athlete is informed of their positive test, too much time has passed to identify the exact source of contamination with the certainty that the rules demand," Schrager added. "That is not a failure of honesty or effort, it is simply too much of a burden to be met in every case.

"This is one of the most difficult periods of my life. Losing my contract, my team and the structure that had long shaped my purpose and identity left me facing a level of uncertainty I had never known."

Schrager, who has cerebral palsy, described the impact on her mental health as "significant and at times overwhelming" - yet vowed to make her comeback in 2027.

Article continues below

She secured ParalympicsGB's first medal of the 2024 Games, claiming silver in the women's C1-3 3,000m individual pursuit.

She later won two gold medals at the Para-cycling Road World Cup in May 2025 in the C2 class – before being suspended just a month later.

Sean McCann missed out on a medal as he finished last in the men's 400m freestyle swimming final at the Commonwealth Games. McCann, 21, finished 12 seconds off the pace for Scotland in a race which saw Australia take gold, silver and bronze.

Sam Short topped the podium, with Elijah Winnington and Benjamin Goedemans finishing second and third respectively. England's James Guy narrowly missed out on the bronze model after being bumped down to fourth late in the race. Northern Ireland's Daniel Wiffen came fifth.
