World.title: Ministry bill will enhance consumer rights on warranties and repairs
World.content:
The Justice Ministry has drafted a bill giving consumers stronger warranty and repair rights for white goods and electronics, particularly with products from outside the European Union.

The bill aims to make electronic products more durable and improve the rate at which products are repaired rather than replaced. Warranty periods will be extended to three years and repair options, both spare parts and services, will need to be available inside Estonia, regardless of an item's country of origin.

Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200) said under current rules getting a defective household appliance repaired generally costs more than buying a replacement. One of the bill's objectives is consequently to encourage manufacturers to produce more durable products.

"Manufacturer liability will be extended to three years, and if something needs to be repaired that is not the result of damage caused by the user but stems from poor product quality, then the manufacturer will indeed have to cover the cost of that repair. The manufacturer's warranty will also be extended from two years to three years if the product is repaired," Pakosta told ERR.

Jüri Rütman of the service center at computer repair store Netiabi said while there is interest in getting devices repaired, there are cases where buying a new device makes more sense. Availability of spare parts depends on a device's age too, he noted. "With products up to 10 years old, manufacturers can generally still provide spare parts, but not for older devices. Around 10 years is the dividing line," Rütman said.

Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200). Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Minister Pakosta said the changes included in the bill should help alleviate the spare parts problem.

"In addition, manufacturers must ensure that those spare parts are actually available. There have been situations, particularly in Estonia, which is a small market, where spare parts have simply not been available. Repair technicians themselves have told us this," she said.

Pakosta said the bill would not affect Estonian manufacturers. Instead, Estonian household appliance retailers are likely to rely more on manufacturers that have a representative within the EU.

"If your product breaks down within three years of purchase, the manufacturer will actually be obliged to repair it. If the manufacturer or its representative does not have a presence in the European Union, then the seller must arrange for repairs. That means selling products for which no repair arrangements exist will become less attractive for retailers," Pakosta said.

The bill will need to be approved at the governmental level and then pass a Riigikogu vote before entering into law.

World.title: Open Narva Days offer peek into lesser-known sides of Estonian border city
World.content:
On August 14–16, Narva invites visitors to explore the Northeastern Estonian border city anew through local-led tours, stories and lesser-known corners tourists often miss.

The weekend's #VisitNarvaNext program includes seven locally-curated themed tours, focusing on personal stories rather than just historical sites.

Participating tours, some of which are exclusive to Open Narva Days, will be offered over three days in combinations of English, Estonian and Russian.

Among them are walks through childhood memories of Narva in the 90s, family histories preserved through photos and letters and a boat trip along the Narva River led by mayor and historian Katri Raik.

Other tours look at the city through the varied perspectives of a journalist, local fishers and other residents that have shaped the city.

The riverfront during Narva River Day in 2023. Source: Dmitri Fedotkin/ERR

A new "antitour" geared toward adults will also offer participants more direct conversation about life in a border city, Narva's complex identity and how locals see and experience today's changing world.

While in town, visitors can join tours of Narva's Town Hall, Narva Estonian State High School and the casemates, or walkways, of Victoria Bastion, part of the city's surviving 17th-century fortification structures.

Places are limited, so organizers recommend registering in advance. The full schedule and event details are available on Fienta.

World.title: Large number of Elron trains sitting idle at Tapa station
World.content:
Around a dozen of Elron's new Škoda trains are sitting idle at Tapa station despite a shortage of locomotives. Issues with the new rail traffic management system are behind the delays, Estonian Railways said.

The new high-speed locomotives were supposed to start carrying passengers between Tallinn and Tartu a year and a half ago. €82 million has been spent on the procurement of the new trains so far, with €60 million outstanding.

While the hope had been that the new trains would begin operating in the direction of Tartu from July this year, this has been put back six months and they remain at Tapa, a major rail junction.

Railtrack operator Estonian Railways' (Eesti Raudtee) Technical Director Arvo Smiltinš said the delays are the result of several factors. "The railway between Tapa and Tartu is single-track, and we cannot simply close it to train traffic. Finding those compromises is one of the key reasons why the work has not progressed according to the original schedule," he told "Aktuaalne kaamera".

Around a dozen new generation Elron trains are in sidings at Tapa junction, awaiting traffic management and other issues to be ironed out. Source: ERR

Problems have arisen with fine-tuning the traffic management system developed specifically for Estonia, he added.

"We have now introduced the new traffic management system on the section between Aegviidu and Tapa, and it has experienced technical teething problems that we need to resolve to avoid the same issues on the sections that follow," Smiltinš explained.

At the same time, the existing fleet has been diminished due to maintenance issues.

"As is well known, two trains that served long-distance routes were damaged at the end of last year and are still undergoing repairs. Across our entire diesel fleet we can offer roughly 3,000 seats, and about 375 of those are currently unavailable because the trains are being repaired," Elron board member Märt Ehrenpreis said.

Around a dozen new generation Elron trains are in sidings at Tapa junction, awaiting traffic management and other issues to be ironed out. Autor/allikas: ERR

While the renovation work is due to be finished by the end of this year, there are outstanding issues with operating permits too, so the new locomotives will not go online until "some time next year."

Smiltinš acknowledged that the original renovation schedule had been too optimistic, but said the work was now progressing well. He also said Elron had simply ordered the trains too early.

Ehrenpreis rejected this. "I won't comment on that, but I think we ordered the trains at the last possible moment. In reality, manufacturing and procuring trains is a very lengthy process," he said. The procurement had been a favorable deal under market conditions and the locomotives could not be obtained at that low of a price today, Ehrenpreis added.

World.title: 60% of Iraqis have access to safely managed drinking water
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Around 60% of Iraq’s population has access to safely managed drinking water services, according to data from UN-Water and the Our World in Data platform. The figures highlight both the progress Iraq has made in expanding access to clean water and the significant challenges that remain.

The data comes as more than 2 billion people worldwide still lack access to safe drinking water at home, underscoring the global scale of the water security challenge.

According to the report, Iraq’s 60% access rate places it below many developed countries but ahead of several developing nations.

Among the countries with higher access rates are:

Japan: 99%

Italy: 97%

Ireland: 96%

Iran: 94%

Meanwhile, Iraq outperforms several developing countries, including:

Guatemala: 49%

Ghana: 43%

Indonesia: 30%

Guinea-Bissau: 24%

The report notes that safely managed drinking water involves more than simply having access to a water source.

Under the United Nations’ definition, drinking water must come from an improved source, be available on the premises, accessible whenever needed, and remain free from contamination. These standards form part of Sustainable Development Goal 6, which aims to ensure universal access to clean water and sanitation.

The report highlights that most countries in Europe, North America, and Australia have achieved access rates close to or at 100%, reflecting decades of investment in water infrastructure.

By contrast, many low-income countries—particularly in Africa—continue to record access rates below 20% due to inadequate infrastructure, limited funding, rapid population growth, and the growing effects of climate change.

For Iraq, expanding access to safely managed drinking water will require continued investment in water treatment plants, distribution networks, sanitation systems, and ongoing maintenance of existing infrastructure.

The report emphasizes that improving access to clean drinking water delivers benefits beyond basic services. Reliable water infrastructure helps improve public health, reduces the spread of waterborne diseases, supports education, and contributes to long-term economic development. As a result, expanding access to safely managed drinking water remains a key priority for achieving sustainable development and improving quality of life.

World.title: Kuwait to reopen Abdali border crossing within 48 hours after drone attack
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) – Kuwait will reopen the Abdali border crossing with Iraq within the next 48 hours, Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Yousef Saud Al-Sabah announced on Saturday, stressing that a recent drone attack on the facility will not disrupt passenger movement or bilateral trade.

The announcement came during Al-Sabah’s visit to Iraq’s southern Basra province, where he met Governor Asaad Al-Eidani to discuss border security, bilateral relations, and regional developments.

Speaking after arriving at the Safwan border crossing, Al-Sabah said the Abdali crossing would resume operations within two days, allowing the movement of travelers and commercial goods between Iraq and Kuwait.

“The Abdali border crossing will reopen to passenger and trade traffic within 48 hours,” he said, thanking Basra Governor Asaad Al-Eidani and describing relations between the two countries as rooted in brotherhood.

He emphasized that Kuwait and Iraq would not allow attempts to create division between the neighboring states.

“Whatever happens, we will remain neighbors and brothers,” Al-Sabah said. “We will not allow anyone seeking to spread discord between Iraq and Kuwait, and we will work to stop any attempts to fuel tensions from the very beginning.”

The Kuwaiti interior minister confirmed that authorities are still assessing the damage caused by the drone attack, which targeted the Abdali border crossing on Thursday.

However, he stressed that the repairs would not delay reopening the crossing. “The damage is being evaluated and will be repaired as quickly as possible,” he said. “This does not prevent the crossing from resuming operations. Traffic must continue.”

According to Al-Sabah, the crossing will be reopened in time to facilitate travel for Iraqi visitors and Kuwaiti pilgrims heading to Iraq during the Arbaeen pilgrimage season.

Basra Governor Asaad Al-Eidani welcomed the Kuwaiti delegation, describing the visit as a message of solidarity between the two countries. “Iraq, after the fall of the previous regime, should be a country of peace and friendship for all neighboring nations,” Al-Eidani said.

He acknowledged that both Iraq and Kuwait have been affected by wider regional instability despite not being direct participants in the ongoing conflict. “Sometimes mistakes happen because of irresponsible actions by individuals,” he added. “However, those incidents should not affect the strong relationship between our two countries.”

Al-Eidani also said the visit demonstrated the commitment of both governments to preserving regional stability and strengthening bilateral cooperation. Kuwait’s Ministry of Defense confirmed on Thursday that the Abdali border crossing had been targeted in a drone attack.

Officials said the incident caused only material damage, with no casualties reported. Specialized teams were immediately deployed to secure the site and remove drone debris.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed that explosions were heard on the Kuwaiti side of the border, while Iraq’s Safwan crossing in Basra remained unaffected and security conditions there were stable.

Following the attack, Kuwaiti authorities temporarily closed the Abdali crossing as a precaution. The latest developments come only weeks after tensions between the two countries following the fatal shooting of Iraqi fisherman Najm Abdullah by the Kuwaiti Coast Guard in early July.

Surviving fishermen later told local media that they were detained in Kuwait for six days and alleged they were subjected to mistreatment during interrogation before being released through Iraqi diplomatic efforts.

The incident prompted Iraq’s Basra Provincial Council to call for Abdullah to be officially recognized as a martyr and urged stronger measures to protect Iraqi fishermen operating in regional waters.

Despite those recent incidents, Saturday’s meeting between Iraqi and Kuwaiti officials underscored both governments’ commitment to maintaining strong bilateral relations and ensuring that security challenges do not disrupt cooperation between the two neighboring countries.

World.title: Strait of Hormuz crisis reshapes regional trade as Iraq faces growing economic pressure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The ongoing disruption in the Strait of Hormuz is doing more than slowing maritime traffic. According to Iraqi economic expert Manar Al-Obaidy, it is fundamentally redrawing trade routes across the Middle East, shifting commercial activity away from the Gulf and toward the Eastern Mediterranean.

In an analysis of first-half 2026 trade data, Al-Obaidy argues that the crisis has accelerated changes in global supply chains, creating new winners while exposing structural weaknesses in Gulf economies—particularly Iraq, whose economy remains heavily dependent on oil exports passing through the strategic waterway.

According to Al-Obaidy’s analysis, trade between China and several Gulf countries has fallen sharply during the first six months of 2026. Trade with Iran declined by 60%, while Iraq recorded a 55% drop. Saudi Arabia also experienced a significant decline of 48%, reflecting the growing reluctance of shipping companies and importers to rely on routes exposed to security risks in the Gulf.

At the same time, countries positioned along alternative Mediterranean trade corridors have seen remarkable gains. China’s trade with Syria surged by 281%, while trade with Jordan increased by 30%, Egypt by 25%, and Turkey by 10%.

The figures suggest that companies are increasingly redirecting cargo through safer maritime and overland routes rather than relying on the Strait of Hormuz.

Al-Obaidy believes the changes extend beyond a short-term shipping crisis. He argues that the current trends raise broader questions about whether global trade is entering a long-term transition toward new East-West logistics corridors.

While security concerns remain the immediate driver, businesses may continue using alternative routes even after tensions ease because they provide greater predictability and lower geopolitical risk. That shift could permanently alter regional trade patterns, even if it comes with higher transportation costs.

For Iraq, the consequences extend far beyond reduced shipping volumes. The country depends on oil exports for more than 90% of government revenue, with most crude shipments traditionally passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Any prolonged disruption directly affects public finances, budget planning, and the government’s ability to fund salaries and infrastructure projects.

However, Al-Obaidy warns that a second, potentially more serious challenge is emerging. As Asian buyers diversify their energy supplies, China and India could increasingly source crude from Africa and South America instead of relying as heavily on Gulf producers. If that trend continues, Iraq risks losing market share in some of its most important export destinations.

The shift also threatens Iraq’s broader ambition of becoming a regional logistics hub. As cargo increasingly flows through Mediterranean ports and neighboring countries, Iraq risks being bypassed in emerging trade networks.

That could reduce opportunities to expand non-oil exports, attract logistics investment, and strengthen its position as a transit corridor linking Asia and Europe. Without strategic adjustments, the country could find itself marginalized in both energy markets and regional trade.

Despite the risks, the changing trade landscape also presents Iraq with opportunities if policymakers act quickly. Accelerating the Development Road Project could position Iraq as a major land bridge connecting the Gulf with Turkey and Europe, offering an alternative to vulnerable maritime routes.

Expanding rail infrastructure, modernizing border crossings, and improving customs efficiency would strengthen Iraq’s competitiveness as regional supply chains evolve.

At the same time, investing in the ports of Umm Qasr and Al-Faw, together with logistics zones and industrial parks, would allow Iraq to capture greater value from transit trade rather than relying almost exclusively on oil exports.

Diversifying export markets and encouraging domestic manufacturing would also reduce the country’s exposure to external shocks, while expanding renewable energy and natural gas production could lower dependence on imported fuel and strengthen long-term energy security.

Al-Obaidy’s analysis suggests that the Strait of Hormuz crisis is more than a temporary geopolitical dispute. Instead, it may represent the beginning of a broader realignment in global trade, one that favors flexibility, diversified transport corridors, and resilient supply chains.

For Iraq, the message is clear. The country cannot control regional conflicts, but it can decide how it responds to them. Whether Iraq emerges stronger or becomes increasingly vulnerable will depend on how quickly it adapts its infrastructure, diversifies its economy, and positions itself within the new geography of international trade.

World.title: Iraq seeks Iranian assurances for oil tankers as Hormuz crisis threatens state revenues
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has asked Iran to guarantee the safe passage of Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, as ongoing maritime disruptions threaten the country’s oil exports and place growing pressure on government finances. The request was reportedly made by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi during his visit to Tehran on July 23, according to sources cited by the U.S.-funded outlet Alhurra.

The visit marked Al-Zaidi’s first trip to Iran since taking office in May and came just days after his official visit to Washington, highlighting Baghdad’s efforts to balance relations with both regional and international partners amid escalating tensions in the Gulf.

According to the report, Al-Zaidi asked Iranian officials to ensure the safe passage of tankers transporting Iraqi crude through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most strategically important shipping lanes. However, the sources said Tehran did not provide a clear answer, leaving the request without either formal approval or rejection.

Furthermore, the report suggested that Iran may be reluctant to respond positively because of Baghdad’s recent strengthening of ties with the United States. That includes the signing of several major agreements with American companies during Al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington, a development that could complicate Iraq’s efforts to secure Iranian cooperation on regional security issues.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran came only days after his July 13–18 trip to the United States, where he met President Donald Trump and announced a new strategic partnership between Baghdad and Washington. The U.S. visit was the prime minister’s first major international tour since assuming office and focused on expanding economic and security cooperation.

During the Tehran visit, Al-Zaidi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and both sides signed several agreements and memorandums of understanding. At the same time, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi delivered what many observers viewed as a carefully worded political message, stating that Iran “does not need messages or intermediaries because circumstances are changing rapidly.”

Meanwhile, the Iraqi government rejected reports published by The New York Times claiming that Al-Zaidi had carried a U.S. proposal for a ceasefire to Tehran. Officials insisted that the visit was instead aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and protecting Iraq’s national interests amid growing regional instability.

The request to Iran reflects the growing importance of the Strait of Hormuz to Iraq’s economic stability. More than 90% of Iraq’s government revenue comes from oil exports, and the majority of those shipments pass through the narrow waterway before reaching international markets.

Before the latest maritime crisis, Iraq exported roughly 90 million barrels of crude oil each month through the Strait of Hormuz. However, shipping activity has declined sharply as security risks intensified. According to vessel tracking data cited in the report, only one oil tanker crossed the strait on July 23, compared with three the previous day, marking one of the lowest daily figures in months.

The report also noted that Iran has continued targeting commercial vessels with missiles, drones, and unmanned boats despite a memorandum of understanding signed with the United States in June. As a result, Washington has increased military pressure in an effort to safeguard international shipping routes.

The slowdown in exports is already creating wider economic concerns for Iraq. Reduced oil revenues could affect the government’s ability to finance public-sector salaries, maintain budget spending, and support essential public services, particularly if disruptions continue over an extended period.

In addition, the uncertainty has contributed to fluctuations in the Iraqi dinar against the U.S. dollar, while Iraq’s electricity sector remains under significant pressure during the summer months. Continued dependence on imported Iranian natural gas has also increased concerns over possible power shortages, especially as electricity demand remains high.

According to the report, many Iraqis have once again begun relying on family and tribal support networks to cope with worsening economic conditions. While those informal systems have helped communities navigate previous crises, analysts warn they may not be sustainable if the current situation persists.

Consequently, prolonged pressure on household incomes, combined with rising economic uncertainty, could increase public frustration and revive the kind of demonstrations Iraq witnessed during previous waves of economic and political unrest. For now, Baghdad continues to pursue diplomatic efforts aimed at protecting its energy exports while seeking to shield the country from the wider consequences of regional conflict.

World.title: JD.com partners with Iraq’s GINI to expand e-commerce offerings
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China’s JD.com has partnered with Iraqi digital commerce platform GINI to increase access to its goods in Iraq, marking the latest step toward developing the country’s rapidly expanding e-commerce industry.

The deal would integrate JD.com’s product catalog into GINI’s digital marketplace and the SuperQi app, providing Iraqi customers with greater access to items from one of China’s top online retailers.

The agreement aims to establish a direct supply chain between JD.com and the Iraqi market, thereby enhancing product availability and facilitating cross-border online buying.

GINI, an Iraqi digital commerce and market automation platform, combines merchants, delivery providers, and payment services in a unified ecosystem, allowing companies to manage sales, payments, and logistics.

JD.com, founded in 1998, is China’s largest retailer by revenue and one of the country’s leading e-commerce companies, with a vast logistics network that enables rapid order fulfillment across China and international markets.

The agreement comes as Iraq’s e-commerce sector grows, along with rising internet penetration, digital payment adoption, and government efforts to modernize the economy and encourage more private sector investment in technology and digital services.

Baghdad has increasingly pushed to recruit multinational technology businesses and digital commerce platforms as part of larger attempts to diversify the economy away from oil, generate private-sector employment, and enhance access to products and services via online markets.

World.title: Houthis say hit Saudi Arabia as Trump weighs harder Iran strikes
World.content:
Sanaa – Tehran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabia on Saturday as US President Donald Trump mulled fresh strikes on Iran in the deepening Middle East war.

The US military broke its daily announcement of fresh strikes on the Islamic republic on Saturday, following 13 nights in a row hitting military targets there.

Trump said he had not yet decided whether to launch major strikes on Iran, hours before the conflict widened across the region with Yemen’s Houthi rebels claiming a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan.

The Houthis had accused US ally Riyadh of a “dangerous escalation” after it struck military targets belonging to the group on Friday, following the rebels announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.

The flare-up marks a new front in a war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.

Riyadh did not immediately comment on the Houthis’ Ansarollah media post on Telegram on Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in Jizan.

But Riyadh’s civil defence agency issued brief warnings to residents in the city, as well as Yanbu, early on Saturday.

The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.

The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

– ‘Tipping point’ –

The escalation came after Trump said he would hold off on a major operation as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington.

“No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if he had made a decision on hitting Iran hard, for now dialing back reports that he was increasingly frustrated with the war and mulling a large-scale military operation.

“Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”

Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left a ceasefire in tatters.

The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November.

Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.

The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members.

The Iranian military said Friday it had carried out attacks targeting US military assets in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said they had targeted an Amazon data center in Bahrain, according to state media, though neither the US tech giant nor Bahrain has commented on the claim.

There was also no confirmation from the United States of any targeting of its facilities or personnel.

In Bahrain, sirens sounded again early Saturday, the interior ministry said, urging residents to take shelter.

– ‘I trust them’ –

Trump also insisted Russia and China were not arming Iran, despite reports both were feeding Tehran intelligence to target US forces.

“President Xi (Jinping) said he will not partake, and President (Vladimir) Putin said the same thing… I trust them,” Trump told reporters.

“I don’t think they’d want to have me disappointed.”

On the diplomatic front, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Kyrgyzstan.

Wang called for a resumption of negotiations and the implementation of a memorandum of understanding aimed at easing tensions in the Middle East and the Gulf region, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.

That referred to the preliminary deal aimed at ending the war which has collapsed as the foes fight to break a deadlock over the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as conflict deepens
World.content:
Sanaa – Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East war expanded.

Riyadh struck Houthi military targets in Hodeida on Friday, with rebel media reporting two wounded after the Yemeni group announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hit its ships.

The flare-up marks a new front of the war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route.

The rebels had accused Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” and said its actions “will not go unanswered”.

The Houthis’ Ansarollah media said on Telegram early Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan on the Red Sea.

Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim.

But Riyadh’s civil defence agency had issued brief warnings to residents in Jizan and Yanbu early Saturday for “potential danger”, only to lift the warnings minutes later.

Similar warnings have been issued in the past when missiles or drones were fired at the kingdom.

The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets.

The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

– Blockade –

The Yemeni security source, who requested anonymity, said the Saudi strikes targeted a telecommunications building near Hodeida’s port and a naval base at Ras al-Kathib in Hodeida.

The Houthis’ al-Masirah television channel said two people were wounded — a worker in Hodeida and a woman on Kamaran island.

It said a telecoms building had been hit in Hodeida.

On Monday, the rebels had warned in a radio message to ships that they would target vessels “belonging to (the) Saudi enemy” that do not comply with their blockade.

Saudi state media cited a transport authority official on Friday as saying “the vessel (NCC MASA), belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea today… resulting in minor damage to the vessel’s hull”.

The ship resumed its course, the SPA added.

Red Sea access has become vital for Saudi Arabia to keep shipping oil as traffic in Hormuz is disrupted.

In April and May, all of Saudi seaborne crude exports departed from its Red Sea port of Yanbu, according to Kpler data. It represented 92 percent of all seaborne crude exports in June and 78 percent so far in July.

The Houthis have been at war with Yemen’s government since 2014, in a conflict that has killed hundreds of thousands of people.

The recent exchange of fire threatens a 2022 truce that has held despite expiring.

World.title: Mixed day for global equities as oil prices retreat
World.content:
New York – The main international oil contract Brent North Sea fell back under $100 Friday after surging past the key milestone the previous day on escalating Middle East strikes, helping US and European stock markets stabilize.

Brent dropped about four percent to under $97 a barrel, having soared seven percent Thursday. The key US contract, West Texas Intermediate, declined more than three percent after having gained more than six percent on Thursday.

The sizeable jumps had come after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea, potentially opening a new front in the Middle East war.

Despite the United States launching fresh strikes Friday on Iran, there was relief on markets that some ships were still able to pass through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a crucial passage into the Red Sea.

“Ships with Saudi crude are still crossing…so for now, it is not a full blockade, reducing a bit the risk of an even tighter oil market,” Giovanni Staunovo, a commodities analyst at Swiss bank UBS, told AFP.

A Houthi spokesman said Friday that the rebels were not blocking traffic through the strategic strait.

On Wall Street, both the Dow and S&P 500 rose, while the Nasdaq retreated again, with semiconductor shares enduring another round of selling.

Angelo Kourkafas of Edward Jones described markets as buffeted by uncertainty over unpredictable geopolitical events and questions about how the Federal Reserve will weigh the latest jump in oil prices.

At the same time, “the bar is set high and there is also some skepticism about the sustainability” of this week’s lofty corporate earnings, Kourkafas said.

David Morrison at Trade Nation said expectations that the US Federal Reserve could hike interest rates at its meeting next week have risen from 13 percent last week to 30 percent currently.

“Perhaps more seriously, the CME’s FedWatch Tool shows a 90 percent probability of at least one 25-basis point rate hike before year-end,” he said.

Besides the Fed, next week’s schedule includes another heavy calendar of quarterly results featuring tech giants such as Amazon and Apple, as well as major industrial players including Boeing and Ford.

With tech stocks not as predominant in Europe, that region’s main stock markets advanced on Friday.

Asian stock markets followed the sell-off Thursday on Wall Street as world markets were battered by a perfect storm of the resurgent Middle East war, the spike in oil prices and concerns about the artificial intelligence boom.

World.title: Sarnath joins Unesco World Heritage list
World.content:
Sarnath gets global recognition Sarnath gets global recognition Sarnath gets global recognition 1

2

NEW DELHI: India's ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List Saturday, becoming India's 45th site to receive this recognition. India ranks sixth globally and second in Asia Pacific Region for the most number of 'World Heritage Sites'.Sarnath was included in the tentative list in 1998. The proposal to include the site in the list of world heritage was sent for consideration of the World Heritage Committee in Jan 2025. The decision on the inscription was taken at 48th session of the committee under way in South Korea.The Unesco tag will cover the Chaukhandi Stupa and archaeological remains of Sarnath, located about 626m apart. The Chaukhandi Stupa commemorates Buddha's meeting with his five companions after enlightenment, while the archaeological complex includes Dhamek Stupa, Dharmarajika Stupa, the Ashokan Pillar and extensive monastic remains.PM Modi lauded the historic milestone on X. "A proud moment for every Indian! Delighted that Sarnath has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List."

World.title: IFF says govt order to GitHub on BitChat unconstitutional, demands its withdrawal
World.content:
The app allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages

NEW DELHI: Digital rights advocacy group Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has termed govt's order directing GitHub to remove the source code repositories of Bluetooth-based messaging app BitChat "unconstitutional and authoritarian".In a statement Friday, IFF said the order, issued by Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the home ministry, directed GitHub to disable access to three BitChat repositories, including the Android application and release files, within three hours. It added that the order warned the platform of loss of safe harbour protection and possible criminal prosecution for non-compliance.It argued govt relied on Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act and Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021, instead of the dedicated blocking framework under Section 69A of the IT Act and the Blocking Rules, 2009, that require procedural safeguards such as recorded reasons and an opportunity for hearing.IFF also contended that the order did not identify any specific unlawful content in the repositories and instead objected to BitChat's ability to function during internet shutdowns through Bluetooth mesh networking. It said anticipating potential misuse of a communications tool was not a sufficient legal basis for ordering its removal.The foundation criticised the three-hour compliance window, saying it effectively denied GitHub meaningful legal recourse, and demanded that govt withdraw the notice.

World.title: From one paper leak protest to another: Full circle for Dharmendra Pradhan
World.content:
NEW DELHI/BHUBANESWAR:

's resignation Saturday marks an unusual stumble in a political career that appeared to be headed towards more important destinations.

The architect of BJP's maiden victory in

and facilitator of a series of wins elsewhere was first catapulted into the limelight while leading an ABVP-backed agitation in 1996 against an alleged Class XII question paper leak in Od-isha, during which he was injured in a police lathicharge.

Four years later, he won the Pallahara assembly seat on a BJP ticket. He became president of BJP's youth wing, BJYM, in Odisha in 2001 and was elevated as party national secretary in 2002. In 2004, he was appointed BJYM national president.

It was also the year he first entered Lok Sabha from Deogarh, when BJP and BJD were allies. Disappointment followed when he lost the assembly poll from Pallahara in 2009 after delimitation abolished the Deogarh LS seat and the alliance collapsed.

Pradhan made a comeback when he was appointed co-in-charge of BJP's campaign for 2010 Bihar assembly polls, which BJP swept along with JDU. His nomination to Rajya Sabha from Bihar was seen as a just reward. As election in-charge of Bihar for the 2014 LS polls, he was crucial to NDA's sweep of 31 of its 40 LS seats.

Reforms in education under Pradhan

In 2014 he was inducted into Modi's first cabinet as MoS with independent charge of the petroleum ministry, despite resistance.





Three years later, he was cabinet minister.

Amid the controversy over gas pricing, Pradhan launched a clean-up drive and put an end to the complete drip of corporate houses in the sector. His ministry's Ujjwala scheme helped expand LPG access. His work helped him get the education portfolio in 2021.

Pradhan's background as a grassroots worker also made him a crucial player in political battles. In 2022, he was made the party's election in-charge in UP, where BJP won 255 of 403 seats. In 2024, he successfully contested from Sambalpur. Though he retained the

in Modi's third term, the reward was seen as less than what he deserved, considering he was the architect of BJP's organisational base in Odisha - a state where the party swept to office for the first time.

But things have been challenging for him since then, with paper leaks in 2024 and 2026, as well as the botched-up OMR rollout by CBSE.

In between, he delivered a success in Haryana in 2024, and Bihar, where he was BJP's election in-charge in 2025.

World.title: Left scores win, despite its shrunken presence, through its student organs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi, to pressure govt to give into the demand of getting Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.

In fact, AISA members, president Neha Bora and Manish Kumar and Ameen Amitoj, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.

The victory of their student outfits, which made common cause with those sections of Gen Z, who are usually not receptive to their "class warfare" trope, could act as a compensation of sorts for the Left in an electorally bleak season, marked by routs in Kerala and West Bengal.

Earlier, in another instance of them successfully using their tactical intelligence, the Left, through its farmers' wings, influenced the protests in Punjab against farm sector reforms laws enacted by Modi govt, which had to junk them.

If AISA, SFI and AISF were a vocal presence throughout the protest, their mother outfits CPI(ML), CPM and CPI, in that order, complemented the effort on the ground by goading the opposition to support the CJP-led protests.





According to Left functionaries, who have been part of the demonstrations, when the Left-aligned students groups joined the students' protest led by CJP, they were drawn into the fold organically and not perceived as people just jumping in for credit as these students have been raising issues around the flaws in the examination system and the challenges through their unions.

All 15 MPs belonging to the Left joined the students to protest the police action against them during the march to Parliament on July 20.

They also ensured there was no dilution of the demand for Pradhan's resignation.

CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya agreed that the success of the protests has given the Left a fillip. "This movement has re-energised ongoing struggles across the country for democracy, justice, and the defence of the Constitution." He called upon INDIA bloc to carry the energy, resolve, and democratic spirit of this movement into Parliament and intensify the struggle for affordable and quality education for all.

CPM general secretary M A Baby said Pradhan's resignation was the first step. "Congratulations to Abhijeet Dipke and CJP, to SFI, AISF, AISA, and lakhs of students and young people for their courage and determination which has won this historic victory. We demand comprehensive reform: scrap NTA! Take back NEP!" CPM said.

"It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant govt, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students' movement has defeated the arrogance of BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures," CPI general secretary D Raja said.

World.title: PM Modi is India's past, protesting youth the country's future, says Rahul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Asserting that "time has come to remove this govt",

's

said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. He added that the "past can never fight the future". Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister

's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness".

Rahul said students' agitation has issued a warning that if BJP-RSS continue to run the govt like their personal fiefdom, they would face a stir 10 times more intense than what is happening now. He accused RSS of hollowing India from inside like termites. He said Pradhan's resignation is a signal to other communities that are being "oppressed" by Modi govt, that fighting the govt is a wise step.

Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said, "Force was used against them.

But the youth did not bend; govt had to bend." She said she had been wondering for the past 10-12 years, "When will we wake up and realise what is being done to our country?" She said the youth are reclaiming their country.

Party MP K C Venugopal said, "A massive salute to millions of students across country who compelled this govt to bow down to their will."

Rahul said that Pradhan was a symbol of corruption and destruction of world-class education system, and "it is good that he is gone".

World.title: Bill proposes 3-month deadline for HCs to dispose of paper leak appeals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists.

This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.

According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.

What changes in New Bill

As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years.

In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years.

In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.

For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.





The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.

It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.

It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.

World.title: Amit Shah & other top BJP functionaries call on Pradhan at his residence to show solidarity
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A steady stream of leading BJP figures, including home minister

, visited

's residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned as education minister owing to student protests over the NEET paper leak.

Besides Shah, finance minister

and commerce and industries minister

Piyush Goyal

were among the key Union Cabinet members who met Pradhan, who has handled crucial political assignments, including state elections.

Shah said Pradhan helmed "bold reforms" by implementing NEP, placing emphasis on mother tongues, and making exams more inclusive and student-centric. He added, however, that the country and the young generation were more important to BJP than any office, saying, "Modi govt respects the youth's sentiments and is committed to necessary reforms against paper leaks."

Party president Nitin Nabin said BJP "stood firmly" with Pradhan."He played a pivotal role in reforming India's education landscape and successfully implementing the landmark NEP... Prioritising larger interests, his decision to step down reflects the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life," Nabin added.

The tributes are a firm indication that Pradhan remains a valuable figure for BJP despite his exit owing to political necessities.





Defence minister Rajnath Singh said Pradhan's tenure reflected his commitment to transforming India into a developed nation. "His contribution to public service has been inclusive, foresighted, and aligned with the aspirations of a new India," he added.

Another ministerial colleague, Kiren Rijiju, praised Pradhan for his dedication to strengthening India's education ecosystem. "Leading such a critical sector demands immense persever-ance, and he embraced it with courage and clear vision," he said.

World.title: Ram Temple donation theft row: UP govt reconstitutes SIT; IG Kiran S to lead probe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Acting on the Supreme Court's directions, the

government has constituted a new

(SIT) led by senior IPS officers to investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.

The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S, with Deputy Inspector General Somen Verma and Ayodhya Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Gaurav Grover as members. It replaces the earlier SIT, which was headed by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and included Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar among its members.

The apex court had, during a July 13 hearing, expressed the view that allegations involving theft and financial irregularities required investigation by experienced police officers.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan directed the state to form a fresh SIT under a senior IPS officer and submit a status report by July 27.

The case centres on allegations that offerings made by devotees at the Ram temple were siphoned off instead of being deposited through the prescribed process.

Investigators probing the case earlier examined CCTV footage, donation registers, cash-handling records and financial documents, besides questioning temple staff.





Their preliminary findings indicated suspected irregularities in the counting and deposit of donations.

The investigation led to the arrest of several accused, while police seized cash, vehicles, investment documents and other assets allegedly acquired using the misappropriated funds. Investigators also analysed bank transactions and other digital evidence to trace the alleged money trail.

With the new SIT now taking over the probe, the Uttar Pradesh government is expected to place its findings before the Supreme Court in a status report on July 27.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest updates: President accepts Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Pralhad Joshi to take charge of Education Ministry
World.content:
This live blog is closed

Dharmendra Pradhan, in a post on X on Saturday (July 25, 2026), announced that he has tendered his resignation from the post of Union Education Minister.

The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.

Prime Minister Narendra is yet to provide any public comment on this.

Also Read | The ‘cockroaches’ who refuse to crawl away

Loud cheers erupted at the Cockroach Janata Party protest site at Jantar Mantar after its founder Abhijeet Dipke announced Mr. Pradhan resignation announcement before the gathering, declaring that the movement had achieved its first breakthrough. Mr. Dipke, however, made it clear that the agitation would continue.

With Mr. Pradhan stepping down, Dipke described it as the movement’s “first victory” but reiterated that the remaining demands — compensation for the bereaved families and action against those responsible for the alleged paper leak — were yet to be fulfilled.

World.title: Will push for lowering contesting age for MLA, MP to 21: Telangana CM Revanth
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that the State government would soon adopt a resolution in the Assembly urging the Centre to amend the Constitution to reduce the minimum age for contesting Lok Sabha and Assembly elections from 25 to 21 years, arguing that India’s Gen Z deserves greater representation in legislatures and governance.

Addressing a massive gathering of students and youth in Hyderabad after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation, Mr. Reddy said the Telangana Assembly and Legislative Council would be convened in the first week of August to pass a resolution seeking an amendment to lower the minimum contesting age for Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies to 21 years. The resolution would then be forwarded to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Recalling constitutional reforms that expanded youth participation, the Chief Minister said former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment, recognising the voice of young India. He also referred to the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments introduced during the tenure of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, which enabled 21-year-olds to contest elections to local bodies.

World.title: Enemy’s intentions unchanged, proxy war still a challenge: Rajnath
World.content:
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who toured Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh’s Drass on Saturday (July 25, 2026), said the intentions of the enemies have not changed, and the proxy war remains a security challenge in the region.

Without naming Pakistan, Mr. Singh, while speaking at Shaurya Bhoj in Drass, said, “As we celebrate the Kargil War victory, we have to remind ourselves of the challenges. The intention of our enemy remains the same. Proxy war is still used as a tactic. Our Army is ready to foil these nefarious designs,” said Mr. Singh.

The Defence Minister arrived in Srinagar on Saturday (July 25, 2026) morning on a two-day tour of the region. He was received by J&K Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha. Officials said they discussed the current security situation in J&K, especially in the wake of the Anantnag attack that left one policeman dead three days ago.

Later, Mr. Singh visited the war memorial at Ladakh’s Drass on the eve of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas. He paid tributes to the soldiers who laid down their lives in the line of duty in the 1999 Kargil War against Pakistan, as he attended the ‘Shaurya Sandhya’.

“It’s these sacrifices that make people of India feel safe. When oxygen levels dropped in 1999, the guns of our soldiers did not fall silent till the Tricolour was unfurled as a mark of victory. We are proud of the valiant soldiers and their degree of courage,” said Mr. Singh.

He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had ensured that the morale of soldiers remains high. “We are investing in modernisation of equipment and training. We are hopeful to see the Indian Army among the leading forces in the world,” he said..

Mr. Singh said the Indian armed forces were fully prepared to face every challenge posed by the country’s adversaries. “India’s military remains vigilant, battle-ready, and capable of protecting the nation’s sovereignty,” he said.

He said no one dares cast an evil eye on India as long as the patriotism and determination of the country’s soldiers remain unshaken, adding that their sacrifices ensure every Indian can pursue dreams without fear.

Ten families of Kargil War bravehearts were felicitated on the occasion. Commemorative events were held at ‘Yudh Sansmaran’ at Lamochen View Point, where the Kargil War veterans and families of fallen soldiers remembered the sacrifices made during Operation Vijay. A documentary and special presentations highlighting the valour of 40 war heroes were screened during the event.

Mr. Singh will be the chief guest at the national homage ceremony on July 26. He is expected to lay a wreath at the war memorial, interact with Veer Naris and Veer Maas, inaugurate a virtual walkthrough portal, and flag off the Shaurya Vijay Yatra motorcycle rally.

World.title: Haryana completes SIR phase-I; over 33 lakh names left out due to relocation, death, duplication
World.content:
With Haryana completing the first phase of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the State, the names of 33,84,568 electors went unrecorded as a result of permanent relocation, absence, death or duplicate entries.

Haryana’s Chief Electoral Officer A. Sreenivas said that the first phase of the SIR in the State has been completed and the draft electoral roll will be published on July 31, which will be made available on the official website as well as at all designated publication centres.

Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Sreenivas said that 20,629 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) distributed enumeration forms to more than 2 crore electors, out of which over 1 crore enumeration forms have been digitised.

“However, the names of 33,84,568 electors could not be recorded. Of these, 13,75,278 had permanently shifted, 7,66,205 were found to be deceased, 2,04,916 were already registered as electors, 9,36,646 electors were found absent, while 1,01,523 electors did not submit their enumeration forms due to other reasons,” he said.

He said that claims and objections can be filed from July 31 to August 30. “If the name of any elector does not appear in the draft electoral roll to be published on July 31, he or she may submit Form 6 to get the name included again. The name will be included in the final electoral roll,” he said.

“The name of any elector will not be deleted without giving an opportunity of hearing. If an elector is aggrieved by the decision of the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), an appeal may be filed before the District Magistrate within 15 days. If the grievance still persists, a further appeal may be filed before the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days,” he added.

The final electoral roll will be published on October 3, he said. He said that 37,055 Booth Level Agents (BLAs) appointed by various political parties are also assisting in the process. “These include 19,051 appointed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), 15,818 by the Indian National Congress, 1,476 by the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), 54 by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), 314 by the Communist Party of India (CPI) and 342 by the Jannayak Janata Party (JJP),” he said.

World.title: AISA calls for ‘Bihar Bandh’ on July 25, against police lathi charge on protesting students
World.content:
Protest marches and dharna were witnessed in several districts of Bihar on Friday (July 24, 2026) by the students and locals demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET paper leak.

Protesters holding banners, posters and placards carried out the protest marches in Vaishali, Muzaffarpur, Khagaria, Darbhanga, Bettiah (West Champaran), Supaul, Jamui, Samastipur, Madhubani and Buxar. In Vaishali, the protesters burnt the effigies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dharmendra Pradhan.

Last evening, in Jehanabad, police had to open 20 to 30 rounds of fire after protesters pelted stones on the official residence of the District Magistrate. Jehanabad SP office on July 24, 2026, released the photographs of over a hundred protesters urging locals to identify them so that legal action could be taken against them.

Jehanabad SP Kota Kiran Kumar today carried out a flag march along with 300 police jawans in view of the ongoing security challenges and protests in the State. Mr. Kumar asserted that the police are on high alert to maintain peace and public safety. He added that police from all stations in the district are continuously patrolling major intersections.

Patna police has also published the photograph of over 100 miscreants who vandalised public properties and beat up police and press personnel.

“On July 22, 2026, during the demonstrations that took place in Gandhi Maidan and the Income Tax Circle areas of Patna district, some unruly elements attacked the police force. Police vehicles were damaged. Ordinary citizens and media personnel were also assaulted with sticks, batons, bricks, and stones, “a press statement from the office of Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Patna stated.

It further said, “Through social media, such miscreants are being identified, and their photos/pictures are being published. Please assist the Patna Police in identifying these unruly elements. Identify the individuals according to the serial number of the photo and provide this information to the Patna Police at 0612-2217000, 9939919191, so that legal action can be taken against them.”

Heavy deployment of the police force has been done in all districts of Bihar after All India Students’ Association (AISA) called for a Bihar Bandh on July 25, 2026, against police lathi-charge on the students in Patna on July 22.

Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Bihar State Secretary Kunal has strongly condemned the police lathi-charge, firing and arrests of the students protesting against alleged NEET paper leak across various districts of Bihar, stating that such suppression of democratic rights is a matter of grave concern for any democratic system.

He noted that police action has been taken against peaceful student protests in 18 districts of Bihar so far, making it clear that the government is choosing the path of repression instead of acknowledging its failures.

Mr. Kunal asserted that AISA State Secretary Dipankar Mishra and State Vice-President Saba Afrin have been arrested by the police in Patna and there has been no information regarding their whereabouts.

“It is a blatant violation of the rule of law and civil rights. The police must immediately share the details of their arrest and release them unconditionally, along with all other arrested students,”Mr. Kunal said.

He mentioned that fabricated cases have been filed against several AISA leaders and activists, including CPI(ML) MLC Shashi Yadav and MLA Sandeep Saurabh.

He added that the CPI(ML) will extend its moral support to the Bihar Bandh.

“The party appeals to students, youth, parents, and citizens who believe in democracy across the state to support the Bandh. At the same time, the student community is urged to carry forward their movement in a completely peaceful, democratic, and lawful manner so that their voice reaches out to the entire society with greater strength,”Mr. Kunal said

World.title: West Bengal Assembly passes Bill depriving panchayat pradhans of financial powers
World.content:
The West Bengal Legislative Assembly on Saturday (July 26, 2026) passed the West Bengal Panchayat ( Second Amendment), 2026 Bill depriving elected representatives of panchayats of financial powers.

The bill was passed with 169 votes polled in favour of the bill, while 13 MLAs voted against it. 32 MLAs did not participate in the voting process.

The proposed legislation seeks to amend several provisions of the West Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973, with the stated objective of ensuring administrative stability, uninterrupted public service delivery and smoother functioning of rural local bodies.

The statement of objects and reasons of the legislation says that the bill was brought to ensure the stability of panchayat bodies for the time bound delivery of services to the public at large.

The bill provides for the prescribed authority to appoint an extension officer, or an officer of a higher rank, as Administrator for a maximum period of 30 days if both the pradhan and the deputy pradhan remain absent for more than 15 days and no elected member is willing to discharge the responsibilities.

The bill also addresses situations where no gram panchayat meeting is held for two consecutive months due to the absence of the pradhan and deputy pradhan. In such cases, the panchayat secretary, with the approval of the Block Development Officer (BDO), will be authorised to convene the meeting.

Participating in the discussion, Panchayat Affairs and Rural Development Minister Dilip Ghosh said the Bill does not intend to curtail the constitutional powers of elected panchayat heads.

“Rather, it is aiming at curtailing the authority for corruption and commission against rural civic services. Henceforth, the elected panchayat heads will only approve any proposal. But the Bill will be cleared and sanctioned by the bureaucrats,” he said.

The State Panchayat Minister alleged that in many instances where pradhans have refused to sign work-related documents due to issues regarding alleged ‘cut-money’ (kickbacks). He stated that the objective of the amendment is to curb such irregularities. Mr. Ghosh claimed that among all States in the country, it is only in West Bengal that panchayat pradhans possess such financial powers, and that economic interests have been a major factor behind the violence witnessed during panchayat elections.

A few days ago, the State government issued a notification depriving panchayat pradhans and elected representatives of powers to issue birth and death certificates.

Despite the change in the regime in West Bengal, most of the panchayats and local bodies are administered by the Trinamool Congress. The Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal argues that most of the panchayat pradhans have stopped performing their duties and thus such legislative changes were necessary.

World.title: Youth have reclaimed Gandhi’s idea of India: Mehbooba Mufti
World.content:
Former J&K Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti on Saturday (July 25, 2026) congratulated the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) for its “success” and said it has managed to “reclaim Mahatma Gandhi’s idea of India”.

“For more than a month, these youths were out without food. They adopted a Gandhian style. The biggest success is that these youths reclaimed Gandhi’s idea of India. They have rejected and dismissed divisive politics, especially Hindu-Muslim politics. It has given hope, otherwise amid a sense of dejection. It seems the future of India is in safe hands,” said Ms. Mufti.

She praised the CJP for allowing her to speak at the Jantar Mantar recently and backed its demands for compensation to the families of students who ended their lives and an apology for the atrocities allegedly committed on the youth by the Delhi police.

“We were warmly welcomed despite the narrative of Kashmiris being separatists and anti-nationals. It was heartening to see that this generation puts more focus on the future of the country than the Hindu-Muslim divide. I am hopeful what J&K students faced outside will also stop now,” said Ms. Mufti.

She said what started in Kashmir is now reaching every corner of India. “Peaceful protests silenced with lathis. Constitutional promises broken. Institutions weakened. Today, minority rights are under threat. Tomorrow, no citizen’s voice or vote will matter. The unity seen at Jantar Mantar is the real backbone of this nation. This isn’t just a struggle for one community; it is a fight to save humanity, democracy, and the soul of India,” said Ms. Mufti.

Ms. Mufti also raised the issue of Muslim women, saying these women were facing “harassment for wearing a burqa or hijab.“ You cannot praise Islamic heritage and culture on visits abroad while turning a blind eye to the harassment of Muslim women at home. True empowerment isn’t a slogan for foreign trips. It is guaranteeing safety, dignity, and religious freedom for every woman in India,” she added.

World.title: Not security concerns, but erosion of political capital of the ruling party led to Pradhan’s resignation
World.content:
The primary reason behind Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation on Saturday (July 25, 2026) was not security concerns, but the erosion of the ruling party's political capital caused by the burgeoning, organic crowds at Jantar Mantar, government sources told The Hindu.

The continuous sit-in by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which started on June 13, was called off on Saturday (July 25, 2026) after the government accepted its demands, including withdrawal of criminal cases against protesters.

Taking cue from the July 20 march to Parliament, during which several unarmed protesters were beaten up by the police, the Union government had made elaborate security arrangements for the next few days to contain the crowd at Jantar Mantar, the protest site in the heart of Delhi.

An analysis of the social media chatter, which was found to have unsavoury remarks, particularly against the Prime Minister, after videos of police excesses on students and young people surfaced, also played a role in government conceding to the CJP’s demands, the foremost being Mr. Pradhan’s resignation.

Diverse crowd

“The police were underprepared on July 20 as the crowd, which reached the protest site following a call given by the CJP, was much beyond the initial estimate. However, there was little concern that the protests could lead to a Nepal- or Bangladesh-like situation, as the crowds were largely organic and socially diverse. Some unruly elements were mixed in the crowd, but the police had taken adequate measures post-July 20,” said a government source.

At least eight Internet shutdown orders were issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) between July 20 and July 25, blocking communication in a radius of 1.5 km around Jantar Mantar.

An Internet ban was imposed briefly on July 18, too, when activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been on a hunger strike for more than 20 days, was forcibly removed from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital by the police.

“The police were prepared to hold and manage the crowd at Jantar Mantar for the next few days, coinciding with the ongoing session of the Parliament. The gathering was largely peaceful, and the possibility of unruly elements wanting to take advantage of the situation is always there,” said another government source.

Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda said on Saturday (July 25, 2026) that the CJP delegation submitted a written proposal covering cases related to the agitation along with its five-point charter.

“The government assured the team that no action will be taken against the organisers and protesters, and no new cases will be registered in connection with the agitation. It also expressed condolences to the families of the students who lost their lives and assured them of the highest possible compensation as per the rules,” Mr. Nadda said, adding that discussions will continue with the delegation. This was Mr. Nadda’s third meeting with the delegation.

For a first information report (FIR) to be cancelled, the Delhi Police will have to withdraw the case and send a report to the court saying that it no longer wishes to pursue the case.

World.title: Twisha Sharma case:  Why court rejected mother-in-law’s bail application
World.content:
A district court in Bhopal Friday rejected the bail application of retired judge Giribala Singh, holding that releasing her at this stage could influence evidence in the dowry death case of her daughter-in-law, model-turned-actor Twisha Sharma.

The court observed that the prosecution’s apprehension that evidence could be affected if Giribala Singh was granted bail “cannot be said to be unfounded” and noted that the case diary contained sufficient material indicating her alleged involvement.



Rejecting the plea, First Additional Sessions Judge Ram Pratap Mishra took note of material collected during the investigation, including WhatsApp chats, call-detail records and statements of the deceased’s family members. “The material available in the case diary indicates the involvement of the applicant/accused in the offence. The alleged offence is a serious crime against a woman and is punishable with imprisonment for life. If the applicant/accused is granted the benefit of bail, there is a possibility that the evidence may be influenced,” the court said.

World.title: Elections are won with votes, respect earned through public service: V-P C P Radhakrishnan
World.content:
HIGHLIGHTING THE role of public service, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan on Saturday told a group of new Rajya Sabha MPs that while elections are won with votes, respect is earned through public service.

Inaugurating a two-day orientation programme for the newly-elected MPs, the Rajya Sabha Chairman underscored the need for commitment to the people and the Constitution.



“Debates, discussions or even disruptions, it must always lead to a decision,” he said.

“C P Radhakrishnan noted that while elections are won by votes, respect is earned through public service. He urged mem­bers to remember that every question asked, every law ena­cted, every policy framed, and every debate participated in has the potential to transform lives,” as per a statement. Deputy Cha­irman Harivansh said they had the “right to hold government accountable, offer constructive criticism, guide the government onto the right path… ” it said.

World.title: Operation Vijay: The Regimental Medical Officer who chose to return to action
World.content:
During Operation Vijay in 1999, Captain (now Brigadier) Jyoti Prakash served as the Regimental Medical Officer of an elite PARA unit in the Mushkoh Valley. A paratrooper, he had volunteered for PARA and in the thick of war this soldier-doctor sustained a splinter injury at Bakharwal. For most that would have been reason enough to recover at the field surgical centre and remain away from further danger. The captain chose otherwise.

As the nation observes Kargil Vijay Diwas on July 26, the 55-year-old Brig Jyoti Prakash, Prof and Head, Department of Psychiatry at Armed Forces Medical College, Pune, shared how important it was to ‘be the healing touch, lead with calm hands and wear the uniform with pride.’

Brig Prakash (who was a Captain then) was 28 years old and would share the same ethos of PARA units operating beyond enemy lines — courage, endurance, brotherhood and mission-first commitment. In the thick of the war under heavy artillery shelling and in unforgiving terrain, the 28-year-old stood shoulder to shoulder with his men as a die-hard paratrooper and a soldier- doctor.

At Bakharwal, he sustained a through-and-through splinter injury caused by hostile action. Evacuated by helicopter to the nearest Field Surgical Centre, his wound was cleaned, explored and stitched. However despite excruciating pain and injury he boarded the next sortie back to Bakharwal. For a soldier, shedding blood in the line of duty is among the highest honours of service. As an RMO,he was able to save the lives of many combatants injured in the line of fire and ensure that the unit remained battle-ready. While he settled in Pune in 2019, colleagues said Brig Jyoti Prakash remains a unique case of an elite paratrooper and Regimental Medical Officer who went beyond the call of duty and saved lives.

Kargil Vijay Diwas honours the courage, sacrifice and determination of the Bravehearts of Operation Vijay. As the nation remembers their historic victory, Col Satish Malik who lost his leg to a mine blast in an op area has over the years dealt with challenges. His leg below the knee had to be amputated and fitted with a prosthetic one at Pune’s Artificial Limb Centre. But not once did he look behind and pursue activities with a vigour that led him to overcome physical barriers, drive cars and ride his motorcycle around the country.

Col Malik continued in the Armed Forces till 2008 and took voluntary retirement. Along with a partner he set up a risk management consultancy firm and is part of the Phoenix Braveheart rider group that bikes all over India , Bhutan and Nepal. “I never felt handicapped,” he said adding that his guiding mantra has always been ‘I won’t give up until I have truly tried’. This belief has guided him through life, helping him face challenges with determination and never give up without trying and during the Chief of Naval Staff, Indian navy, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan’s visit at ALC, Pune both shared light-hearted moments as they recalled their days as batch mates at NDA.

World.title: 4th Justice G P Singh Memorial Lecture: Consuming chicken biryani no offence… dissent essence of democracy, says Justice Bhuyan
World.content:
Saying that there was “no law prohibiting consumption of chicken over the Ganga river”, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan of the Supreme Court on Saturday criticised the arrest of youngsters for consuming chicken biryani while breaking their fast. “I am sure consuming chicken biryani is not an offence. It can’t be an offence…they were arrested for that very reason and they had to remain in jail for three months,” he said.

Speaking at the 4th Memorial Lecture of Justice G P Singh at the National Law Institute University (NLIU), Bhopal, Justice Bhuyan said peaceful protest is central to a democracy but ordinary acts of dissent are increasingly being treated as criminal conduct. “The right to express one’s views and to demonstrate peacefully are fundamental freedoms of the citizens. Debate and dissent are the essence of democracy. Unfortunately, even normal activities are being criminalised,” he said.

Referring to environmental protests and student demonstrations, he said, “People who come to voice their anguish over environmental degradation, which is a reality, are chased away as if they are criminals. Students protesting in campuses are arrested and they do not get bail for 30-40 days.” He added that students are often suspended as well, forcing them to approach courts before they can resume their education.

Justice Bhuyan questioned whether courts, through restrictive bail conditions, were also discouraging dissent. “These issues raise serious questions… though the courts are responsive and do grant bail, many a time it is belated. But it is the restrictive conditions which are imposed while granting bail that are causing the greatest concern. By such restrictive orders, are the courts indirectly telling the citizens or discouraging the citizens not to express their dissent?” he said.

Referring to the Supreme Court’s 2024 judgment against punitive “bulldozer justice”, Justice Bhuyan said the ruling was welcome but had come “two years too late”.
